Kylian Mbappe has revealed he came close to joining Liverpool as a teenager before his rise to the top of the sport, with his mother and agent keen for him to move to Anfield.

Mbappe said in an interview with The Athletic that he came close to joining the club in the summer of 2017, when he had a private meeting with then-Reds boss Jurgen Klopp on a private jet over the south of France.

His mother and agent Fayza Lamari was also present for the meeting, with Klopp trying to persuade Mbappe - then aged 18 - to move to Anfield rather to French giants Paris-Saint Germain.

Mbappe said: “It was while I was playing in Monaco. I had to take a decision. And yes, I was close to Liverpool. My mum was a big fan of Jurgen Klopp and the favourite destination for my mum was Liverpool. She wanted me to go there.

“I didn’t listen because I wanted to play in my city, Paris. I didn’t want to leave my country before I was someone. But yes, my mum was always saying ‘Liverpool – you’re going to be there, playing at Anfield, it’s going to be insane for you.’ I was like, ‘OK!’”

He recalled how Lamari went to Liverpool early in negotiations and was drawn to the feel the club had. “She was like, ‘It’s a wonderful club, everybody’s so kind, it’s a family club, a big club.’

“She went to Anfield and fell in love with it. She watched a few games alone, to feel the atmosphere, because she wanted to imagine me in this stadium.

“All the time we were talking. [I would say:] ‘What do you think, Mum?’. She’d say, ‘For me, you have to go to Liverpool’. I said, ‘OK, OK, OK!’ because Jurgen Klopp was an amazing manager. I met him and had a wonderful relationship with him. I had big respect for him.”

Klopp revealed details of the meeting on the private jet earlier this year, telling German outlet Magenta TV that it was “the most expensive non-transfer we ever made”.

Ultimately the journey from Blackpool to Nice, and his mother’s enthusiasm, proved insufficient to sway Mbappe. He joined PSG initially on loan for the 2017-18 season before signing permanently the following year, remaining in Paris until a move to Real Madrid in 2024.

He recalled: “In the end I took the decision to go to PSG because for me, born and raised in Paris, there was no better feeling than to show I could be a star in my home town.”

Tensions are high ahead of an international soccer doubleheader between Ireland and Israel, with both nations using inflammatory language about their opponents amid protests in Dublin urging a boycott of the matches.

The games taking place on Sunday and Oct. 4 — both on neutral territory — are going ahead following a request by the Football Association of Ireland that UEFA, European soccer’s governing body, suspend the Israel Football Association in protest of Israel’s military action in Gaza. It was rejected by UEFA.

Campaigners stepped up their attempts to get the Ireland team to not play the first match between the teams in Hungary, with a group gathering outside the team’s hotel in Dublin on Monday evening.

More than 160 Irish sportspeople have signed an open letter issued by the Irish Sport for Palestine Group, urging the FAI to reconsider its decision to go ahead with the fixtures and saying: “With this moment you have an opportunity to do the right thing.”

After announcing his squad, Ireland coach Heimir Hallgrimsson said: “Without going into individuals, none of us feel comfortable playing in these games but once we have decided to play them, we all stick together and play as one.”

Hallgrimsson, who is from Iceland, also was asked about how his players would stay focused on the games. He answered: “We’re not playing with genocide, we’re playing against genocide. We’re playing against Israel, we’re not playing with Israel.”

Israel has denied deliberately targeting civilians and pushed back on accusations, including from rights groups, that it committed genocide in Gaza.

Israel has come under genocide accusations repeatedly since launching the war in Gaza in response to the Hamas attack on Israel on Oct. 7, 2023. The International Court of Justice is hearing an ongoing genocide case against Israel filed by South Africa.

On Monday, the Israel FA responded to Hallgrimsson’s comments with a post on social media that read: “We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way.

“Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by (Hallgrimsson). We’re not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we’re playing against the coach who embodies them.”

An October 2025 ceasefire reduced the intensity of the fighting, but Israel has continued to carry out strikes, killing over 1,375 people since the agreement went into effect, according to local health officials.

The nearly three-year Israel-Hamas war has killed more than 73,821 Palestinians, according to Gaza’s Health Ministry. The ministry, part of the Hamas-run government, maintains detailed records viewed as generally reliable by U.N. agencies and international organizations. It does not distinguish between civilians and militants, but says women and children make up around half the toll.

Why Ireland is playing the games

The calls from back home for Ireland to boycott the matches against Israel have been loud.

In a May friendly against Qatar, Irish activists hurled tennis balls onto the pitch in protest. The balls had “Stop the Game” written on them, referring to the upcoming Nations League matches.

The FAI has argued that boycotting the games could damage its chances of qualifying for the 2028 European Championship, which Ireland is co-hosting with Britain, and that it would proceed with the fixtures in order to avoid “significant and lasting harm.”

Sunday’s game will be staged in Debrecen, Hungary, and the reverse game — a “home” match for Ireland — will be behind closed doors in Bačka Topola, northern Serbia.

Ireland opted to stage the game in neutral territory because of what the FAI described as “operational challenges” that could arise if it was played in Dublin.

Israel has had to relocate, often to Hungary, for its home games for security reasons since October 2023, with UEFA having ruled the country cannot host international matches because of the war.

No tickets for either match will be made available to Irish fans.

Two teenagers returning from coaching class in India’s eastern state of Bihar were reportedly surrounded by a group of men who assaulted the boy and molested the girl, sparking widespread condemnation.

The incident took place around 7pm on 19 September in Jamui in India’s poorest state when the two class 10 students were returning from their coaching on a scooter.

Several men surrounded the scooter being driven by the boy, with the girl seated behind him, according to a purported video of the incident that later surfaced on social media.

The boy tells them they study at the same school, and their families know about them, but a person slaps him saying, “then call them”.

In another video, a man can be seen grabbing the boy by his shirt and attempting to pull him.

The boy manages to get rid of the grip with the girl’s help before the two try to escape.

Another man grabs the girl by the neck, lifting her off the ground. The minor could be heard screaming and trying to resist. As the boy tries to intervene and pull her away, a scuffle follows, with one of the men molesting her.

The group forces the duo to repeatedly apologise, and the girl can be heard pleading with the men, promising to not return to the area, with someone in the group eventually heard asking the two to leave, saying “go, go”.

Since the incident, the police have arrested six men, including Nandan Yadav, who was identified as the key accused and was shot in the leg during a chase on Tuesday.

It came after a preliminary chargesheet, known as First Information Report (FIR), was filed in the case, with a special investigations team formed under a Jamui sub-division police officer to identify and apprehend the others involved, reported the Times of India.

The case was registered under the stringent Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, invoked in instances involving abuse of minors.

Jamui superintendent of police Vishwajeet Dayal told Press Trust of India Mr Yadav was the main accused and was hiding near Madwa Hill, where the two students were stopped. Police tried to apprehend him, but he allegedly attempted to flee and was subsequently shot in the left leg.

Among those arrested are three minors and other three are aged between 35 and 40, reported Times of India.

The National Commission for Women – the state women’s rights body – has also taken suo motu cognisance of the incident, demanding “time bound and impartial investigation”, while directing authorities to provide “security, legal assistance and psychological counselling” to the victims.

The police meanwhile have launched action against accounts circulating videos of minors, as Indian laws prohibit the identification of minors and women in cases involving sexual assault. So far, 13 Facebook accounts, 12 Instagram handles and seven Meta accounts have been identified for take down, reported India Today.

The police action comes amid widespread outrage after the clip of the incident was widely shared on social media, drawing criticism from key opposition figures, including leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi. Calling this incident “deeply disturbing”, he wrote: “Who gave these men the right to behave like this? This is not ‘culture.’ It is patriarchy: the belief that any man can police a girl's body, her movement, her choices.”

Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee also condemned the incident, calling it “gut-wrenching” and “shocking”.

“Those who took the law into their own hands in the name of ‘moral policing’ must be held accountable by the police and the law. No society can allow mobs to decide who deserves dignity, who deserves freedom, or who deserves punishment,” she said.

It has also turned into a political flashpoint, with government of the state, headed by prime minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party, is being widely criticised over the response of some of the MLAs to the incident.

Bihar minister Shrawon Kumar was criticised for calling the molestation of the minor an “isolated” incident. “These isolated incidents happen. Those who commit such acts in Bihar cannot escape; strict action has been taken against them in the past as well.”

Local politician and the state’s leader of the opposition Tejashwi Prasad Yadav called the incident a “blot” on Bihar.

“It is really sad they are calling the assault on the girl and boy as isolated. Had the same happened with any family member of any leader, would they have said the same thing? The harassment incident is shameful.”

Bihar sports minister Shreyasi Singh on Tuesday sparked a major controversy after she told India Today that “moral policing can be done in a more decent and elegant fashion, but the way they mishandled and mistreated the boy and girl together is absolutely not tolerable.”

The state has recorded highest number of violent crime incidents in 2024, with 107,303 cases recorded, according to data released this year by the National Crime Records Bureau.

At 12,438 cases, Bihar also recorded the highest number of kidnapping and abduction cases of women, inducing women to compel marriage.

The first phase of an £12.9 million attraction, set to become the UK’s biggest urban farm, is now open in Greater Manchester.

Northern Roots, a new 160-acre development in Oldham, transformed underused land next to Alexandra Park into a “landmark development” complete with Snipe Clough Farm, a four-acre urban agriculture site.

The green space officially opened on Saturday 19 September.

According to Oldham Council, the site gives people the “chance to enjoy nature closer to home, improving local health and wellbeing, supporting education, creating local jobs, and playing an important role in Oldham's ongoing regeneration”.

The project, a partnership between the Northern Roots charity and Oldham Council, plans to increase wildlife habitats by 25 per cent and store 30,000 tonnes of carbon by 2050.

The site includes a new farm-to-fork cafe, outdoor play areas, a forestry skills centre, a network of walking trails and spaces for school visits, community events and performances, following a five-year development.

Northern Roots aims to attract 300,000 annual visitors by 2030 with everything from beekeeping courses to textile classes.

Anna da Silva, chief executive of Northern Roots, said: “This project has always been about much more than creating a beautiful green space.

“We've set out to show what happens when you invest in nature as essential social infrastructure - somewhere that improves health, creates opportunities, restores biodiversity, supports local businesses and brings communities together.”

She added: “Northern Roots belongs to Oldham, but we also hope it becomes an example of what is possible for towns and cities across the UK.”

The site will open under normal operating hours – 9am to 4pm, Thursday to Sunday – from 24 September.

Shelley Kipling, chief executive at Oldham Council, said: “What has been achieved here is truly remarkable. Transforming former industrial land into a vibrant green space that people can enjoy, learn from and benefit from is something that will make a lasting difference to people's lives.”

“Oldham is one of the greenest boroughs in the region, and we want people to enjoy the benefits of having such a fantastic green space on the doorstep. This is a landmark moment for Oldham that complements the wider regeneration of our borough,” he said.

A police officer, charged with the killing of Australian TV presenter Jesse Baird and his new partner Luke Davies, was driven by “jealous infatuation” with his ex, prosecutors told a court in Australia.

The prosecution, represented by advocate Brett Hatfield, alleged that Beau Lamarre-Condon, shot his 26-year-old ex-partner Baird, and the 29-year-old Qantas flight attendant at a home in Sydney in 2024.

The 31-year-old has pleaded not guilty to two charges of domestic violence-related murder and one of aggravated break and enter. He was accused of using a work-issued gun to shoot his ex-partner and Baird’s new partner Davies. He said he was acting in self-defence, the court heard.

The authorities launched a frantic search for the bodies of the couple after bloodied items were found in a bin in Sydney in February 2024. The bodies were subsequently found eight days later in a rural area 200km away, in a surfboard bag.

Mr Lamarre-Condon was sacked by the NSW police after he was charged with the murders.

open image in gallery Condolence books and a poster in honour of Jesse Baird and Luke Davies seen during a public vigil at Green Park on 1 March 2024 in Sydney ( Getty )

In the trial, that is expected to go on for three months, the prosecution described Mr Lamarre-Condon’s “obsessive and jealous infatuation”. The prosecution said it manifested itself in a “range of compulsive behaviour”, escalating to Baird ending all contact in November 2023.

Mr Lamarre-Condon allegedly met Baird in late 2022 but the relationship ended in April 2023. It, however, resumed again in September of that year but things were called off after the TV presenter found that the police officer accessed his phone to delete messages and block people.

The prosecution alleged that on the day of the murder, the accused set up an alarm for 4.30am and sent a text to a friend saying, “I’ll try to call you tonight and update you ... there’s no sign I’m doing it”.

open image in gallery People gather to remember Jesse Baird and Luke Davies during a public vigil at Green Park on 1 March 2024 ( Getty )

After that, he allegedly switched to a burner phone, rented a car, and waited outside his ex’s home disguised as an Uber Eats rider before entering through a key he “surreptitiously obtained”, said the prosecution.

He shot his ex-boyfriend twice in the kitchen, and then his partner Davies “to eliminate him as a witness”, the court was told.

Mr Lamarre-Condon was further accused of breaking into Baird’s home in August 2023, and stealing his phone and wallet.

The investigators were alerted when “significant” amount of blood in Baird’s home and later when the men’s belongings were discovered in a bin near Sydney. Mr Lamarre-Condon handed himself in at the Bondi police station in Sydney.

Donald Trump’s administration plans to spend $100 million on a fleet of intelligence analysts for a previously unreported Immigration and Customs Enforcement unit designed to radically expand the agency’s espionage and surveillance work.

ICE’s Enforcement and Removal Operations, the division responsible for arresting and deporting tens of thousands of people from the country, could hire more than 140 intelligence officers and project managers with “top secret” clearances for an “Overwatch and National Security Enforcement” unit embedded in field offices across the country.

According to the government’s request for information, ICE is expecting to hire government contractors to review data from “classified and unclassified sources.”

Those “Intelligence Research Specialists” will then compile reports on their targets and others “to identify significant changes in activity, recurring patterns, emerging relationships, network activity, potential threat indicators, and other developments relevant to assigned intelligence requirements.”

Agents will also perform “analytical research” to “identify and assess relationships among individuals, organizations, locations, events, activities, data points and other entities” to support ICE arrests, according to government filings.

open image in gallery The Trump administration is mulling a $100 million plan to hire dozens of intelligence analysts with top secret clearances to help track down immigrants ( AFP/Getty )

The $100 million plan follows a massive injection in federal funding for the Trump administration’s mass deportation efforts, a government-wide project that now has tens of billions of dollars over the next several years to recruit and hire ICE agents and expand its detention capacity.

ICE already spends millions of dollars buying up data that it uses for intelligence collection, including pulling from cell phone data and surveillance software to track down and arrest immigrants and monitor American citizens who have criticized the agency.

The agency also has deployed facial recognition technology, license plate readers, drones and other technology to boost arrests. Earlier this year, ICE also proposed spending up to $180 million on “skip tracing services” from bounty hunters, bail bondsmen, debt collectors, repossession agents and other private investigators to track people down.

Under the proposal for “Overwatch and National Security Enforcement” personnel, roughly three to five analysts would be deployed to 27 cities, including New York City, Los Angeles, Atlanta, Dallas, Houston, Miami and San Francisco, among others, along with a project manager based in Washington, D.C.

Those analysts would be expected to hold active “top secret” government clearances and possess extensive professional intelligence experience.

The analysts would be explicitly prohibited from making arrests.

ICE says it launched the Overwatch program “due to the exponential increase of threats and violence against personnel.”

“ICE protects America through criminal investigations and enforcing immigration laws to preserve national security and public safety and employs technology and intelligence techniques to identify, locate and arrest national security and public safety threats,” a spokesperson for ICE told The Independent.

“ICE and its partners need to stay ahead of criminals and terrorists, which evolve just as rapidly as the technology they use to support their criminal activities,” the person added.

The agency is now relying on what it calls an “intelligence-driven approach” to prevent “future attacks through comprehensive intelligence collection and analysis.”

open image in gallery ICE has seen a massive injection of federal funding that has been used to boost recruits and add to a vast arsenal of surveillance and intelligence-gathering tools ( Getty )

The proposal comes just weeks after federal court filings provided a rare glimpse into ICE’s surveillance operations, after the agency was forced to reveal how agents spied on a Minneapolis church despite a court order that called the potential consequences of such an operation “profoundly troubling.”

Documents revealed that undercover ICE officers spied on people who attended church meetings and ran license plate numbers of worshippers’ cars, part of a recently unveiled surveillance campaign that sought to crack down on protests after a surge of federal agents in Minneapolis earlier this year.

Massachusetts Judge F. Dennis Saylor IV blocked the Trump administration’s policy giving agents permission to make arrests inside places of worship earlier this year. Last month, the judge sided with church groups who successfully sued the government and agreed to hold a hearing to determine why ICE should not be held in contempt for violating his ruling.

ICE’s hiring streak has come under renewed scrutiny in the wake of a recent whistleblower report from an anonymous ICE official who was previously tasked with evaluating new recruits.

The official, who no longer works at the agency, warned that the Trump administration’s fast-tracked hiring process exposed the U.S. to “grave national security risks,” The Independent previously reported.

The report follows other urgent warnings from current and former officials who feared that the Trump administration’s hiring surge put thousands of officers on the streets without proper guidance or training.

The latest complaint, filed by a 17-year ICE veteran, alleges the agency was relying on an “unprecedented lowering of standards” to onboard “improperly vetted” candidates who were receiving job offers before they passed any background checks.

The official, who directly oversaw more than 100 employees and evaluated thousands of ICE applicants, was so alarmed by the process that he filed a complaint with the Office of Inspector General in the Department of Homeland Security.

That report follows a similar whistleblower complaint from now-former ICE lawyer Ryan Schwank, who served as an assistant chief counsel and later as a legal instructor at the ICE Academy at the Federal Law Enforcement Training Center.

The academy was “teaching cadets to violate the Constitution, and they were attempting to cloak it in secrecy,” he said earlier this year.

News.title: Tax rises ‘virtually inevitable’ after £8bn borrowing blow
News.content:
Britons have been warned that tax rises are “virtually inevitable” after official figures showed the Treasury has borrowed £8bn more than expected so far this year.

Economists said the Chancellor faced an “uncomfortable” Budget after the Office for National Statistics (ONS) said the deficit between tax receipts and spending stood at £18.3bn last month, £3.5bn higher than expected.

It means John Healey, the Chancellor, has borrowed £77.3bn so far this financial year, which is £8.1bn more than forecast.

Emma Reynolds, the Chief Secretary to the Treasury, warned of “tough decisions” in Mr Healey’s Budget following the publication of the figures.

Thomas Pugh, chief economist at RSM UK said: “The jump in borrowing in August compared to last year sets the stage for what is likely to be a much trickier budget than Burnham or Healey anticipated when they came to power.

“Another round of tax rises in October now looks inevitable.”

Philip Shaw, an economist at Investec, added: “We suspect that some tax increases are virtually inevitable.”

Ruth Gregory, deputy chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said the Chancellor will need to raise up to £14bn to restore the £24bn of fiscal headroom left by his predecessor Rachel Reeves to balance the books.

Ms Gregory said: “The penultimate public finances release before the Budget on October 28 paints a dismal picture.”

The ONS said the government’s debt interest bill soared to £8.8bn last month, which was the biggest August bill since records began in 1997.

So far this year, the Treasury has spent £50bn on debt interest - £2 billion more than forecast in March.

Nick Ridpath, an economist at the Institute for Fiscal Studies, said: “Debt interest spending is a worryingly large share of overall government spending.

“Both higher borrowing costs and higher inflation make life harder for a Chancellor who is looking to bring down borrowing and to spend more on government priorities.”

Higher prices caused by the Iran war mean the Chancellor must pay more interest on the country’s huge stock of inflation-linked debt.

Inflation is also pushing up the welfare bill. The Government spent almost £30bn in August on benefits, up 7pc compared with a year ago.

Despite this, the Treasury continued to see bumper tax receipts. Income tax, capital gains, and national insurance receipts stood at £231bn in the financial year to August.

That is £16.6bn higher than the same period a year ago.

Inheritance tax receipts also grew, rising to £3.8bn so far this fiscal year, a £100m increase compared with a year ago.

Ms Reynolds, the Treasury minister, said: “At a time when debt interest costs billions of pounds that could otherwise be spent on improving lives, we must always know where the money is coming from to pay for public services.

“That is why we are committed to meeting our fiscal rules with a buffer against uncertainty.”

The figures also showed total debt rose to £2.985tn in August, taking the level just shy of £3tn.

Andrew Griffith, the shadow Chancellor, said: “Labour have lost control of the public finances.

“It takes a rare fiscal incontinence to have both the highest tax take in history and see borrowing still shoot up.”

News.title: France releases infertile Asian tiger mosquitoes to fight dengue threat
News.content:
French cities are fighting the growing threat of diseases like dengue, chikungunya and Zika in mainland Europe by releasing millions of sterile male Asian tiger mosquitoes.

Terratis, a new company in the southern city of Montpellier, is breeding infertile males on an industrial scale as a long-term solution to the rapid spread of the disease-carrying insects.

The sterile males are bred at a factory in the southern city of Montpellier and then released in urban hot zones where the mosquitoes are most prevalent. After they have mated, females reproduce only empty eggs for the remainder of their lives.

“By using this technique, the mosquitoes will have no descendants and then, in theory, we can reduce the population with each generation,” said Clelia Oliva, the founder of Terratis.

“We are confident of being able to achieve a reduction of between 70 and 90 per cent in the towns in which we are releasing the sterile mosquitoes.”

The company, which started only two years ago, has experienced a dramatic surge in demand in the last few years as France tries to deal with the invasive species.

News.title: ‘42 surgeries in 48 hours’: Doctors face extreme pressure in South Sudan
News.content:
Dr Mathiang Agany had no idea what was coming.

On a humid morning in April, scores of patients were rushed into his basic hospital in rural South Sudan after a shoot out between rival gangs. As the most senior doctor, Dr Agany, a maternal health specialist, had to perform 42 surgeries in just 48 hours.

Working alongside a second surgeon, a nurse and an anaesthetist, Dr Agany, 44, carefully extracted bullets from the vital organs of nine patients.

In 22 cases, he glued together fractured bones; and in four others he clamped damaged tissues shut and repaired torn organs.

Over the same 48 hour period, he also delivered seven babies through emergency c-sections.

“You are tired... but you can relax later,” he told The Telegraph over a video call.

“My job [was] to keep people alive”.

Separate to the ruinous four-year civil war in neighbouring Sudan, the violence plaguing South Sudan is inter-communal, a self-perpetuating cycle of cattle raiding, territorial disputes and revenge attacks carried out by armed youth militias from pastoral communities known as Titweng (“cattle guard”).

Young children were among the victims, including a four-year-old boy, whose leg was fractured by a gunshot, and a nine-month-old baby girl whose chest was grazed by the same bullet that killed her father.

News.title: Afghan medical students face expulsion from Pakistan
News.content:
An educational lifeline for young Afghan women banned by the Taliban from training as doctors in their homeland is in jeopardy after Pakistan’s medical authorities tried to have them expelled.

Several hundred Afghan female students studying across the border in Pakistan have been threatened with removal, amid rising tensions and tit-for-tat exchanges between the neighbours.

The Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) which regulates medical education earlier this month ordered medical and dental colleges with Afghan students to kick them out.

Within days, major institutions including King Edward Medical University (KEMU), Shaikh Khalifa Bin Zayed Al Nahyan Medical and Dental College, and the Services Institute of Medical Sciences, had ordered Afghan students to leave.

The nationwide order was estimated to have affected around 1,000 Afghan students, with 35 per cent of those thought to be female students.

Provincial high courts have now temporarily halted the expulsion pending further hearings, but Afghan students told The Telegraph they were terrified their careers would be ended.

“The government’s decision aimed to send us to the Stone Age because the Taliban in Afghanistan have banned female education,” said Sabiha Daftani, one of the 22 Afghan students given orders on September 7 by KEMU in Lahore on to leave within 24 hours.

“The fear is constant and haunting us,” she said.

News.title: Michael Carrick will not survive unless Manchester United change
News.content:
But so passive was their football that is the way he felt in the moment. For a club with United’s “attack, attack, attack” tradition – becoming something of a distant memory as seasons pass – that is a damning as it gets.

Neville’s Sky paymasters will be delighted by his emotive, insulting, headline-grabbing language. But he of course exaggerated a point to make a point. United, and Carrick, were, indeed, far too passive, lacking aggression, urgency and belief. They just do not press. United did, for too long, play like a team of dummies.

Against Fulham they almost played walking football until they conceded, desperation kicked in and they chased the game to salvage a late draw.

It begs the question: what is Carrick doing with this team? Yes, he may have been let down by no defensive signings in the summer – even if he must have bought into the plan to prioritise a midfield rebuild – but he is far from absolved from blame.

He will cling to the response to Lisandro Martínez’s own goal, to striking a post twice in the first half from Matheus Cunha and Bruno Fernandes, to managing to avoid a third successive defeat in a week, which would have led to the crisis klaxon being sounded. Carrick can talk about how ridiculous it would be to question his position as head coach. But is it?

We now go into a three-week international break and the Premier League vacuum would have been filled by a debate over Carrick’s future, whether he is up to the job and another existential examination as to where United are heading. And who is to blame.

That still might happen. United did not lose. But they were not remotely good enough, as has been the case for most of the season. Their only league win in five was against newly promoted Ipswich Town, having lost to newly promoted Hull City. They have also drawn at Everton and now at Fulham, who started the day bottom of the table and remain winless. Apart from facing Manchester City, it has hardly been the most taxing of starts. Except they are down in 12th and have not played well at all.

News.title: Alisson’s brilliance takes the breath away to show way forward for Liverpool
News.content:
It proved to be the foundation stone from which Liverpool were able to build and inflict Bournemouth’s first home defeat since January. There are plenty of [valid] questions to ask of Liverpool’s attack at present but, defensively, it is starting to come together.

“It was a really good fight,” Alisson said, in that self-effacing way of his. “But we have to improve a lot – on the ball and sometimes off the ball as well but we improved in the second half. We adapted to the opponent and that’s what we are doing.”

Any manager with a well-drilled defence stands a chance of improving and that is what Liverpool are doing. Only four weeks ago the discussion was about how easy it was for teams to play through their middle – remember that chaotic afternoon at Newcastle to start? – but that is changing swiftly.

Since Iraola replaced Jeremie Frimpong with Araújo at right-back, three consecutive Premier League clean sheets have followed. Araújo, the Uruguayan on loan from Barcelona, revels in doing the dirty work while Jacquet, the £60m signing from Rennes, oozes quality.

“He’s [Jacquet] very young and adapted really well to the Premier League,” Iraola said. “The first games, he was physically feeling the change of rhythm and I had to sub him. This was a step forward. He looked solid until the end. He’s in a good place physically and I hope he can continue his development.”

News.title: All that money spent and Spurs do not have a proper striker or goalkeeper
News.content:
It was an excellent goal, but Kinsky got a good hand to it and a top goalkeeper would have pushed it around the post. On the evidence of the first half, when he made four saves, Suzuki would have also stopped the ball creeping into the net.

Suzuki cost Villa in the region of £30m and he looks a more than able replacement for Emiliano Martínez. Spurs, on the other hand, have not had a top-class goalkeeper since Hugo Lloris and it is a puzzle that so much faith has been placed in Kinsky.

Spurs spent most of the summer firmly denying any links to Jackson before Villa signed him from Chelsea for an initial £47.5m that could rise to £65m. Given the London club paid an initial £75m for Sávio and committed to a £60m obligation to make Omar Marmoush’s season-long loan permanent, Jackson might have been a relative bargain for them.

Asked if Tottenham had made a big mistake by failing to sign a proper number nine, head coach Robert De Zerbi said: “The transfer market was long. The situation changed many times. There was also the financial rules, at the end of the transfer market. And we had to respect the rules.

“We didn’t sell the players who we thought, in the beginning, there was the possibility, the chance to sell. There are a lot of reasons. I think the club and the coach, we are not sleeping, we know the characteristics of the players, we know everything. And if we didn’t make any different decisions, it was because we couldn’t.”

MANCHESTER UNITED expect to lose out on millions with the impending departure of JJ Gabriel.

With Gabriel, 15, expected to head abroad, his perceived quality and potential future value will not be factored into the compensation fee United would be entitled to.



Club sources do not expect to bank a significant figure if or when Gabriel leaves for an overseas club, with the final sum worked out on a standard process.

United could be set to receive as little as £300,000 in training compensation for a player tipped to be worth as much as £100million one day.



If Gabriel moved to a Prem rival a tribunal would decide how much United get – with the club likely to have demanded millions.

Gabriel’s father, Joe O’Cearuill, has likened his development to that of Lionel Messi, Cristiano Ronaldo, Neymar and Lamine Yamal.

Academy figures at United consider Gabriel to be the best 15-year-old footballer in Europe but do not expect him to show his face at the club’s Carrington training complex again.

Gabriel wants to leave after flirting with several elite clubs in recent years and agent Ali Barat lined up talks with Real Madrid and Bayern Munich.

Barcelona have been long-time admirers of Gabriel, who has visited Catalonia at least three times since he joined the United academy. Gabriel was in Barcelona last week.

Despite concerns at United that Manchester City could lure Gabriel, City sources said last week they expected the teenager to leave the UK.

Former head coach Ruben Amorim and director of football Jason Wilcox held discussions with Gabriel last year as United attempted to convince him his long-term future was at Old Trafford.

United agreed to assign Gabriel the brand-conscious number 77 and named him in their Premier League list of squad numbers this season.

The club even downplayed a potential security scare involving one of Gabriel’s party at the FA Youth Cup semi-final at Old Trafford in April.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta ‘agrees new contract with Arsenal with huge pay rise’ that will take Gunners boss beyond decade at Emirates
Sports.content:

MIKEL ARTETA has signed a new long-term contract with Arsenal, reports suggest.

The Spaniard led the Gunners to the Premier League title last season for the first time since 2004.



And he has been rewarded for those efforts with a bumper new deal that is set to include a huge pay rise.

According to BBC Sport, the 44-year-old will see a “sharp” rise in his salary from his current £10million a year plus bonuses.



It will also see him take him up to a 10th year at the Emirates, having joined the club as manager in December 2019.

He appeared to confirm his future when speaking to the media in August, saying of his future: “They [the fans] don’t have to worry about any of that because I want to be here.

“I’m extremely happy and I feel very grateful to work with the people I work with.”

Arteta, who had entered the final 12 months of his deal, was already the Premier League’s best paid manager, dwarfing his colleagues pay in the English top flight.

However, with a new deal now signed off Arteta could fall in line with some of the most well-paid bosses in the world.

SunSport reported earlier this month how only Al-Hilal’s Simone Inzaghi and Atletico Madrid‘s Diego Simeone were on bigger deals than the former Gunners midfielder, £22.34m and £20.19m respectively.

REAL MADRID winger Yan Diomande has baffled fans by SINGING on TikTok after losing the Madrid derby.

Antonio Rudiger scored a consolation goal in the 89th minute but Real could not complete the comeback.

Diomande came off the bench to replace Vinicius Jr in the 54th minute but could not make an impact.



It saw him continue a disappointing start to life at Real Madrid.

The 19-year-old winger has managed just one assist in eight games following his £120million transfer from RB Leipzig.

Fans were quick to comment, with one person writing: “Bro we just lost the Madrid derby…”

Sports.title: Former England manager, 73, who had huge role in David Beckham’s career lands shock job coaching Thailand

EX-ENGLAND star and manager Peter Taylor has joined the coaching set-up of the Thailand national team.

Taylor, 73, earned four caps for the Three Lions, all coming in 1976 alongside two goals.



He was later appointed as caretaker manager of the national team in 2000, taking charge of one game – a 1-0 defeat away to Italy in which he named David Beckham as captain for the first time.

However, Taylor has a vast pool of experience to draw on from a variety of roles.



These include Southend, Gillingham, Leicester, Brighton, Hull, Crystal Palace, Wycombe, Bradford, Dagenham and Redbridge, England Under-20 and U21s, the Bahrain national team and his most recent job with Canvey.

And he will be able to put that experience to good use once again after agreeing to join Anthony Hudson as an assistant with the Thailand national team for the upcoming Fifa Asean Cup.

A statement from the Thailand FA confirmed the appointment of Taylor to Hudson’s staff, where he also joins another English assistant in Kane Wintersgill.

Hudson, 45, said: “Regarding Peter Taylor, we wanted to bring in an additional support member to assist with training.

“Of course, he isn’t coming in to replace anyone or take over anyone’s role, but rather to support the entire staff and help make our work more efficient.”

Taylor’s expertise will particularly be used to enhance the quality of training drills and physical conditioning.

Hudson previously had Taylor as his assistant when he managed the New Zealand team between 2014 and 2017.

It is a role reversal from when Hudson worked as an assistant to Taylor when he managed Bahrain between 2011 and 2012.

Thailand kick off their Asean Cup campaign – being hosted in Indonesia – against Pakistan on September 26.

They also face off against Vietnam on September 29 and then Philippines on October 2.

Sports.title: Biggest executive payouts in football history including Daniel Levy’s Tottenham millions and eye-watering Chelsea fee

DANIEL LEVY pocketed £27million after he was axed by Tottenham Hotspur last year, as he joined a list of massive Prem payouts.

The businessman, 64, had served as executive chairman in North London since 2001, but was ousted after nearly a quarter of a century in September 2025.



The club hierarchy felt that results had become unacceptable under his watch, and that a change was needed.

But the £27m fee is certainly a high price to pay for a shake-up, with the number becoming the second-largest payout ever for a Prem executive, against some stiff competition.



It is just eight million off the record tally of £35m that was paid to Marina Granovskaia in 2022.

The Russian executive was Roman Abramovich‘s right-hand for more than a decade, and was named chief executive of the Blues in 2014.



Her ruthless transfer dealings gave her a fierce reputation at the top level of the game.

But she left following the conclusion of the 2021/22 season after a takeover of the club by Clearlake Capital.

She did not leave empty handed, pocketing the massive sum, in line with her huge impact during her time in West London.

Other club figures, including chairman Bruce Buck, executive Guy Laurence and director Eugene Tenenbaum, split a hefty pot of £14m in compensation following the takeover.

Even split, the payoffs represent some of the biggest the league has produced for the executives.

They are comparable to the fee Donna-Maria Cullen secured during her Spurs exit years later.

Spurs and Chelsea seem to have dominated the payout game in recent years, with Cullen being a close colleague of Levy during his days at the club.

But she elected to step down in June last year in order to spend more time with family.



She will have plenty of cash to splash on her loved ones after receiving a £6.6m payout upon her departure.

That figure dwarfs that of businessman Lee Charnley, whose job was a victim of the Saudi Public Investment Fund’s takeover in 2021.

Charnley stepped away from the club following a handover period, after 22 years in his role as a director.

Sports.title: 'Just getting started' - Pollock signs new multi-year deal with Saints
Sports.content:
Henry Pollock has signed a new multi-year contract extension with Northampton Saints that will see him stay at his boyhood club beyond this season.

Pollock has been a key part of the Saints side since bursting through as a 17-year-old in 2022, delivering a Player of the Match performance during their Gallagher PREM final victory last season.

The back rower already has 13 England caps and five British & Irish Lions caps to his name, with his growing appeal seeing him become the first rugby player to join Eddie Hearn's Matchroom Talent Agency earlier this year.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Eddie Hearn believes Henry Pollock is the future of rugby and says by paying him what he deserves, he can grow the sport to another level

Pollock previously said he had an open mind about next steps in his career, with Hearn labelling him worth at least £1m a year, but the 21-year-old is now looking forward to extending his time at Saints.

In a statement, Pollock said: "I'm massively happy to re-sign with Saints, my boyhood club. It's an exciting place to be right now. We're in a great spot as a team, but it feels like there's still so much more growth in us.

"I'm still young, and we've got a young squad with a brilliant group of lads. Some of my best mates are here, and every day everyone pushes each other to improve and be the best players and team we can be. For where I am in my career, this is exactly where I want to be.

"I feel like we're only just getting started. We won the PREM last season and we want to go again. Winning the Champions Cup is another huge ambition for us. We came so close a couple of years ago, and achieving that together would be incredibly special.

"I just want to enjoy every moment of this journey. I'm playing for my boyhood club, surrounded by great people, and that's something I never take for granted. The connections within this group are what make it such a special place."

Saints' Director of Rugby, Phil Dowson, added: "We're delighted that Henry has committed his future to Saints.

"Over the last few years, everyone has seen the quality he brings on the pitch and the speed of his rise through the game - but just as importantly, he's a young man of outstanding character.

Image: Pollock scored ten tries in 20 appearances for Saints last season

"Keeping someone with both his talent and mindset is hugely important for the club."

'Rugby not used to Pollock and Hearn's contract posturing'

Sky Sports News' James Cole:

"Henry Pollock's transfer stand-off with Northampton divided the club's fanbase. The England flanker is a generational talent. The friction wasn't just financial - it was also cultural.

"Rugby isn't used to the sort of public posturing that Pollock and his agent Eddie Hearn have engaged in over this new deal. It's very un-rugby. Very un-gentlemanly.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rugby star Henry Pollock tries sharing his golf tips using a simulator with Sky Sports reporter Mantej Mann, as the Northampton Saints player likes to play the sport in his spare time

"Some will say that the sport and the attitude of its fans need to evolve. Others will say these are the core values that drive people to play, watch and fall in love with the game.

"The new £400,000-plus contract is likely to represent a three-fold increase in Pollock's salary and make him one of the top-earning flankers in the Premiership.

"It's not the seven-figure sum Hearn thinks his client is worth - but within the parameters of the league and its salary cap, it's an excellent deal. The 21-year-old has the potential to become one of the sport's all-time greats, but he's not there yet."

Sports.title: A mixed Ryder Cup-style team event - could it happen and how would it work?
Sports.content:
Team events are some of the biggest weeks in the golfing calendar, but how realistic is adding a new mixed-gender golf tournament to an already packed schedule?

The Ryder Cup and Solheim Cup both see the best from Europe take on the United States, while the Presidents Cup - live this week on Sky Sports - is a biennial contest between Team USA and an International Team.

The Grant Thornton Invitational is a mixed team tournament taking place every December containing PGA Tour and DP World Tour players, following on from the defunct JCPenney Classic, but is there space for one on an international scale?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charley Hull played alongside American Michael Brennan during the 2025 Grant Thornton Invitational

A mixed team golf event will feature in the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028, while Team Europe captain Luke Donald recently suggested launching a mixed team event that would share similarities with the Ryder Cup and Solheim Cup.

"I'm all for having some events where we're playing together and sharing each other's talents," Donald told the Telegraph ahead of the BMW PGA Championship. "I think it's great to see that.

Image: Luke Donald will captain Team Europe for a third consecutive Ryder Cup next year at Adare Manor

"Who wouldn't want to see a Nelly Korda or Charley Hull playing with a Rory McIlroy, Jon Rahm or Scottie Scheffler - some of the best in the world in the men's and women's games?"

Donald did caveat that the creation of a mixed Europe vs America team event would "take some time to create", plus added it would be difficult to find a time in the calendar for the event.

"It's great in principle but, when you get down to the practicalities of it, where it's going to fit in the calendar?" Ryder Cup-winning captain Paul McGinley told Sky Sports.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the key moments from the final day of the 2025 Ryder Cup at Bethpage Black

"Are the players going to play another team event, particularly when they're probably not going to get paid for it? They're the complexities of it, but it's great in theory.

The Ryder Cup, Solheim Cup and Presidents Cup all traditionally take place in September, following the end of the PGA Tour season, with the DP World Tour schedule the main focus in men's golf during the autumn.

"Maybe they [the PGA Tour] go into a partnership with the LPGA Tour to create something like that," McGinley added. "Whether they do it for the Presidents Cup is doubtful, because they've already said no to that situation evolving.

Sports.title: England fast bowler Wood retires from international cricket
Sports.content:
England fast bowler Mark Wood has announced his retirement from international cricket due to a knee injury.

Wood departs the sport having featured in 38 Test matches where he claimed 119 wickets.

The 36-year-old has not played for England since an eight-wicket defeat to Australia in the first Test of the 2025/26 Ashes series, where - in the series opener - he suffered a recurrence of the same injury which ruled him out of the remainder of the Ashes series.

Image: Mark Wood has announced his retirement from international cricket

In conversation with Sky Sports Cricket's Ian Ward on whether his decision to retire was difficult, straightforward or emotional, Wood replied: "Probably all of them. When you speak to other people, they say it hits you in the face, there's a big feeling around that being it: 'You're done.'

"I've never really had that, I love playing cricket, I love playing for England, that's been something I've felt really strongly about and proud to do. But I've had a lot of injuries.

"I've always found a way where I've believed I'd come back and had that resilience where I'm going to come back again, or I'll be better, or I'll prove somebody wrong again, but this time it's just ground me down really.

"I think it's been a long time since Perth, that was in November 2025 my last game, so it's been a year-and-a-half really where it's just sort of ground me down to thinking: 'I'm never going to get back to this level.'

"I never really wanted to give up England, but the lads that are coming through are doing a fantastic job and the news should be about the lads going to get their contracts and I can just focus on other things."

Wood made his international debut in 2015 in limited-overs cricket, and retires having made 70 one-day international appearances and been a part of England's 50-over World Cup-winning squad in 2019.

He also played 38 T20 internationals and took nine wickets in four games as England won the World Cup in 2022, though injury would deny Wood the chance of playing in the semi-finals and final.

Mark Wood's injury timeline

2015: Left ankle injury, misses third Ashes Test

2016: Ankle problems continue, undergoes surgery and misses England's home Test summer

2019: Side strain, misses first two Ashes Tests

2022: Right elbow injury in the West Indies, requires surgery

2025: Left knee ligament damage, undergoes surgery

2025-26 Ashes: Suffers recurrence of knee injury after returning to Test cricket

2026: Forced into international retirement after recurring knee problems

Image: Wood suffered a number of injuries in his career, to his ankle, elbow and knee among others

Wood: My knee never got right - I rushed back too quickly

Having expressed a determination to play for England again after his latest injury, Australia proved to be Wood's final Test appearance, ending a career beset and curtailed by injury.

"I knew it was bad [knee injury] because I'd had that previous surgery where I was always trying to chase my tail," Wood added to Sky Sports. "Looking back now, it probably never was quite right.

"I was always chasing that dream of, can I physically do this? My ankle problems, my elbow problems, all the rest of them, every time I went back, it felt better. This time, something wasn't quite right.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Mark Wood's five wickets on his return to the England team on day one of the 2023 third Ashes Test

"Since I've had the second operation, things have improved, but not to the point where I believe I could play Test match cricket. I couldn't play 50-over cricket. I mean, I'd still love to play for England for 20 overs, but I think it just feels like a nice time to just say that's a natural end.

"Probably, from my point of view [came back too early and rushed return]. I don't think it's to blame anybody else, it was just, I was desperate to play Perth because it was the fastest wicket there.

"There and in Brisbane, they were the two games I was definitely trying to pencil myself in for.

"I hadn't had much time back on my legs. The warm-up game, my hamstring got incredibly tight because it was looking after my knee, and I think that whole time, when you talk about injury, people don't see the work you're putting in behind you.

"I was desperately trying to get it right. I was taped up to the nines, and I was like a mummy at one point I had that much tape on, but I just couldn't get back quite to that level, and I was just not quite the same in Australia."

Sports.title: Wigan focused on taking on 'battle-hardened' Wakefield in semis
Sports.content:
Wigan Warriors have been there, done that, and got the T-shirt when it comes to making it to the Betfred Super League Grand Final and so their routine is set as they hunt down the treble in 2026.

Wigan have already added two trophies to their cabinet this season having won the Challenge Cup and League Leaders' Shield, with the Grand Final just one step away.

To get there, they need to beat Wakefield in the semi-finals on Saturday September 26, live on Sky Sports after Daryl Powell's side defeated Leigh in the eliminators.

Matt Peet lost a first final as head coach of Wigan at Old Trafford in 2025 against Hull KR, but has already made sure that such heartbreak was fuel to achieve more.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Wigan Warriors thrashed Catalans Dragons 50-12 to finish top of the Super League table and win the League Leaders' Shield. Wigan needed victory in the final round to guarantee top spot

But now, with success firmly in their sights once again, Wigan will keep looking forward while being rooted in the present and ensuring they are firmly focused on the semi-finals.

"We have been through this experience a few times now, learned some lessons, and it is exciting," Peet told Sky Sports.

"It is not a case of that everything we did last year was wrong, some things we got right, we just weren't good enough on the evening.

"We will do what is right for this year's team for this moment on their journey and our journey.

"It is more about looking forward than back."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League semi-final match between Wakefield Trinity and Leigh Leopards

If Wigan were to win the Grand Final, it would mark Peet's 10th trophy since taking over as head coach of his hometown club in 2022, success coming under him at a staggering speed.

However, those statistics are of no importance to him and the most important trophy is always the one next in your sights.

"It is not about that, the next one is always the one," he added.

"We just want to play well in the semi-finals. Not thinking too much about Old Trafford or the trophy or talking about that.

"We know we are going to be up against a very determined and capable team in the semi-finals who have just had a fantastic win.

"They will be battle-hardened and confident so we just have to concern ourselves with that."

O'Neill: Ready to right heartbreak of 2025

2025 was a particularly unique year for Wigan under Peet. They made finals but did not win them as Hull KR swept every honour available.

They also fell to a tough 24-6 loss in the Grand Final, which saw Brad O'Neill sent to the sin-bin for a dangerous tackle.

O'Neill has been one of Wigan's standout performers across 2026, being named in the Super League Dream Team, and would love to right that wrong.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Wigan Warriors thrashed Leeds Rhinos 40-8 at Headingley to move two points clear at the top of Super League with one regular-season game remaining

Indeed, he feels they have put themselves in the best possible position to do exactly that.

"I feel like going away together pre the semi-final when we get the week off is a great opportunity to get some work in but also a good time to bond as well and get away and fresh. Just to enjoy each other's company," O'Neill told Sky Sports.

"We have done it for the last few years and everyone seems to like it.

"I feel like it would mean a lot. Last year was a tough one to take at Old Trafford for myself personally and for the club.

"To put those wrongs right would mean a lot to us all.

"We have given ourselves the best opportunity to do it, we just have to commit now and get through this semi-final first."

Sports.title: Why F1's intense triple header will shape title run-in
Sports.content:
Formula 1 embarks on its first triple header of the season this week with the Azerbaijan Grand Prix the first of three races in as many weekends.

The race on the streets of Baku - which takes place on Saturday rather than the usual Sunday - was originally due to be a standalone event with the Singapore Grand Prix following on two weeks later.

But the moving of the Bahrain Grand Prix to Malaysia in the week between the two events has created the run of three successive race weeks, with two more triple headers scheduled to close out the 2026 season.

So what can we expect from this first Azerbaijan-Malaysia-Singapore triple and what will the world championship picture - which currently sees Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli holding a commanding lead - look like on the other side into mid-October?

Last chance saloon for Antonelli's challengers?

While Antonelli's victory last time out in Madrid was fortuitous thanks to the Virtual Safety Car timing that helped him and hindered McLaren's race-leading Lando Norris, the Mercedes driver was enjoying another strong weekend at F1's brand-new venue and was in position to capitalise on such a slice of luck.

That victory, Antonelli's eighth in 14 races this season, means he arrives in Baku with an 81-point lead at the top of the Drivers' Championship.

Since seeing his title advantage over team-mate George Russell cut to just 25 points at the British Grand Prix at the start of July, Antonelli's lead has increased in each of the last five race weekends to its current season-high total.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nico Rosberg believes the only thing that can stop Kimi Antonelli from winning the World title is himself

Russell remains Antonelli's closest challenger but he all but conceded his hopes of beating his team-mate to the crown after falling more than the equivalent of three races wins behind the Italian by finishing fifth at the Madring.

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton had already effectively ruled himself out after the previous weekend's race at Monza, but was more certain in saying his title hopes were over after brake problems at the Madring saw him register his first DNF of the season.

Hamilton is now 101 points off the pace while fourth-placed Norris, the grid's in-form driver alongside Antonelli, saw his own deficit grow to 106 points on a weekend the reigning world champion was unlucky not to make it three wins in four.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Spanish Grand Prix

All the championship cards appear firmly stacked in Antonelli's favour, not that the young Italian appears to carry the weight of being the clear title favourite particularly heavily.

The 20-year-old has continued to insist he is "not thinking about the championship" in every interview he is asked about it, a mantra that his team boss Toto Wolff says is genuine and the best one for his driver to adopt.

Yet time is obviously running out for any one of the would-be challengers to put a stunning run of form and results together over the final rounds to truly trouble him.

There is still time, though, and with 83 points up for grabs during this first triple header of rounds alone - 75 across the three grands prix and eight for the Singapore Sprint - Mercedes are right to remain cautious - for now.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Toto Wolff reveals Mercedes' team orders strategy

But should Antonelli finish the Singapore weekend on October 11 with a similar or even increased lead compared to the 81-point one he holds now, then the odds on him not becoming the sport's youngest-ever world champion will become very long indeed, even with a maximum of six rounds (and 150 points) left to play for.

What challenges do the next three tracks present?

Kicking off this intense run into the autumn is the Baku City Circuit, a high-speed, wall-lined street track through the middle of Azerbaijan's capital that has often featured on lists of a season's most dramatic races during its first decade on the calendar.

Last year's race - and indeed weekend - certainly fell into that category after a qualifying session that featured a record six red flags and a race, won by Red Bull's Max Verstappen, which saw then-title favourite and points leader Oscar Piastri crash out within six corners. The McLaren driver had also hit the wall in qualifying.

Antonelli, who finished fourth on his F1 debut in Baku last season and took a podium in F2 the year before, will be hoping to avoid those pitfalls as this year's driver to catch on a circuit which Mercedes, like at Monza, are being tipped to be particularly strong.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Look back at some of the most dramatic moments to have taken place around the Baku City Circuit

"Baku is completely different [to Madrid]. Slow-speed corners, massive straights, a little bit lower downforce as a result for those long straights," Sky Sports F1's Nico Rosberg told The F1 Show podcast.

"Engine power is always going to favour Mercedes in that way. We saw it in Monza, so I think Mercedes has to be the big favourite.

"Max Verstappen was fast in Monza, so maybe Verstappen can be the surprise there."

Then, for the first time in nine years, it is on to Malaysia and a Sepang International Circuit that was always a favourite among drivers and fans during its original 1999-2017 run on the calendar.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player With it confirmed that Malaysia will once again host a Formula One race with the relocated Bahrain GP, relive the last time a Grand Prix was held there back in 2017

Ten current drivers were on the grid when F1 last raced there (with Charles Leclerc driving for Sauber in 2017's Friday practice), while Alex Albon and Liam Lawson drove there in junior series.

Antonelli, Russell and Norris are among those whose only experiences of the sweeping layout will have come in the simulation world, although even F1's most sophisticated tools cannot reflect the level of heat and humidity that famously accompanies racing in tropical Sepang.

But oppressive conditions are what drivers are regularly used to anyway in neighbouring Singapore at the Marina Bay Street Circuit, which has certainly been the most physically demanding race of the season in recent times.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On this day in 2017 at the Singapore Grand Prix, Red Bull's Max Verstappen crashed with the Ferrari pair of Sebastian Vettel and Kimi Raikkonen in one of the most dramatic starts ever

What will be new in Singapore this year, though, is that its schedule features the Sprint format for the first time. It will be the sixth and final Sprint weekend of the season.

Sprint weekends by their nature - with a single practice session before the competitive sessions begin - increase the chance of unpredictability and punish any early driver mistakes or missteps on car set-up. Marina Bay, with its omnipresent walls, will only heighten that challenge.

What impact will the latest upgrade packages have?

As has been the case throughout this first season of the sport's new-look cars, the upgrade packages the leading teams bring to each race weekend will continue to have an impact on the pecking order.

Much-improved McLaren will have another package of changes on their MCL40 for Baku, a track where they struggled last year irrespective of Piastri's travails.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris admits team 'were too quick' after missing a crucial VSC pit stop that cost him race lead

Mercedes' long-awaited upgrade will arrive for the following race in Malaysia. The W17 has not been upgraded to any significant degree at a single race since the Canadian Grand Prix at the end of May, an approach which has certainly helped Ferrari, McLaren and Red Bull to catch up.

However, the big question - and, for their rivals, the potential worry - is how much the Silver Arrows' Sepang package pushes them on.

"I think we are bringing a solid upgrade in Malaysia," Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff told Sky Sports F1 in Madrid. "So we've got to survive another race in Baku. Let's see.

"Sometimes it doesn't correlate with the road so well, so I hope that it does and hopefully that puts us on par with the others in terms of upgrades, but you never know."

Mercedes also have an ADUO power-unit upgrade still to deploy this season should they wish, amid suggestions the Silver Arrows could deploy it to coincide with whatever race Russell takes his expected engine grid penalty at.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nico Rosberg discusses what went wrong for Ferrari on a messy weekend at the Spanish Grand Prix

Ferrari - who continue to show flashes of impressive promise but too regularly trip themselves up - and Red Bull - who appear to be getting closer to a first win of the year with Verstappen - will likely have new parts too across the triple header before attention throughout the field fully switches towards the 2027 challengers.

Will Antonelli remain in realistic chasing distance for 2026's final races by then?

Racing on a Saturday! The 2026 Formula 1 season continues live on Sky Sports F1 this week as the Azerbaijan Grand Prix kicks off a triple-header of races, with the Baku race taking place on Saturday at midday. Stream Sky Sports with NOW - no contract, cancel anytime

Sports.title: Jarrad Branthwaite embraces England call-up after injury nightmare
Sports.content:
Jarrad Branthwaite has credited a “complex” rehabilitation programme in Germany, which analysed links between his injuries and his brain and movement, with his return to the England squad.

The Everton defender’s fine start to the season has been rewarded with a place in Thomas Tuchel’s squad for the Nations League fixtures against Spain, Czechia and Croatia. If selected, it will be Branthwaite’s second appearance for the England senior side having been blighted by hamstring and groin problems in recent years.

The centre-half has been ever-present in the Premier League after being restricted to 10 appearances last season by repeat hamstring issues. In the search for a solution to his injury problems, Everton sent the 24-year-old to the MYOS sports and health clinic in Munich at the start of the summer. Branthwaite believes that was a turning point.

“I sat down with the club after the three or four times where I was picking up the injuries,” he said. “It was to look at the wider picture, look at the holistic approach of the body essentially. I went over there for three or four weeks working with a team alongside the club, just to assess different things, and hopefully that has helped. There were a lot of different things looked at like movement patterns, the brain; it was quite complex, but fingers crossed it has worked.”

Branthwaite was carried off in tears after sustaining another hamstring injury in the Merseyside derby defeat by Liverpool in April. The setback ended his season and his prospects of making a late play for the World Cup squad, and Everton’s form also plummeted in his absence.

“It is probably the worst thing as a footballer not to be on the pitch and I think when it keeps happening it is mentally tough because you are sort of doubting your body and going on the pitch wary of what is going to happen. I think now I am in a position where I got managed throughout the pre-season, managed my load well and hopefully I can stay on the pitch this season.”

Branthwaite made his England debut as a substitute in a win against Bosnia and Herzegovina in June 2024, and a recall was a target this season alongside a return to full fitness.

“I found out when I was having breakfast – it was a good start to the day,” the Everton defender said of his call-up last week. “It is a proud moment. Over the last season or so it has been a target of mine. When I have been out and not on the pitch, I wanted to get back playing and give myself the best possible chance to be in and around the England squad after missing such a lot of time.
