Sports.title: Paul Gascoigne reveals the moment he knew Tottenham were ‘going to struggle’ amid 15-year low
Sports.content:
Paul Gascoigne reveals the moment he knew Tottenham were ‘going to struggle’ amid 15-year low

It took Paul Gascoigne one visit to Tottenham's training ground to recognise things would not get better overnight.

Spurs are at real risk of a third-straight season from hell as they sit in last place, having collected just two points from their opening five Premier League fixtures.



2 Tottenham had to wait until the 86th minute against Villa to score their first league goal this season Credit: Getty

It is officially Tottenham's worst start to a Premier League campaign after five games, with a 3-2 loss at home against Aston Villa on Saturday their latest slip-up.

Spurs had the same amount of points to start the 2008/09 season but were three goals better in terms of their differential (-3) compared to now (-6).

Adding to Spurs' woes is that the defeat to Villa was their 22nd loss at home since the start of the 2024/25 campaign.



As brutal as Spurs' malaise has been, Gascoigne, who represented the club from 1988 to 1992, saw it coming.

Paul Gascoigne's verdict on Tottenham's struggles

"Last season was incredible, I went to their training ground, it was unbelievable," Gascoigne said on talkSPORT Breakfast.



"And straight away in my head, I thought, 'They are going to struggle.'

"Because everything is on a plate for them, when I played, the stuff and equipment we had…



"Everything is on a plate for them, but they have got to buck their ideas up.

"The fans were fantastic when I was there, so they've got to do better this season."

As Gascoigne suggested, Tottenham must indeed do better.

2 'Gazza' believes Spurs players are simply too pampered these days Credit: talkSPORT

To do worse would result in relegation, given Spurs have finished 17th for two consecutive seasons.



Life as a Championship club is not something Tottenham has experienced since the Premier League's inception in 1992, with Arsenal, Manchester United, Liverpool, Chelsea and Everton the only other teams not to have been relegated.

Roberto De Zerbi's brutal assessment of Spurs

Gascoigne's brutal assessment of Spurs follows manager Roberto De Zerbi's claim he'd never managed a team so 'fragile' in his 14 years of coaching.

"You're good, or you're bad," De Zerbi told talkSPORT following the Villa loss.

"You can't be very good in the first 30, 40 minutes, and then concede like this in this way.



"It's tough to accept for me."

Who does Tottenham play next?

De Zerbi and his players now have three weeks to stew on the fact they're last in the Premier League due to the international break.

But the fixtures don't get any kinder for Spurs once the Premier League returns, as they travel to Old Trafford on October 10 for a clash against Manchester United.

Sports.title: Runner who saw Norwegian athlete moments before she fell to her death aged 30 pays tribute and admits 'I would give anything for this to have happened to me rather than you'
Sports.content:
A runner who saw Norwegian athlete Ida Amelie Robsahm moments before she fell to her death at the age of 30 has paid tribute to her friend.

Robsahm was training in Romsdalseggen, Norway, on Saturday when she fell, with the altitude 1,329m. The ridge is located 10km away from Andalsnes.

According to Norwegian magazine Kondis, there was a lot of fog and rain with slippery rocks on show in a photo shared by runner Miguel Benitez.

Robsahm is understood to have fallen several dozen metres, and didn't survive her injuries, despite an air ambulance taking her to the hospital.

Benitez was out running with Robsahm, taking a photo of the runner moments before her death, and shared the snap to social media with a heartwarming tribute.

'Hey Ida, after I took that photo of you, we never spoke again,' he wrote on social media.

Tributes have been paid to Norwegian runner Ida Amelie Robsahm after she fell to her death

Fellow runner and friend Miguel Benitez shared a snap of the 30-year-old before she died

'Everything changed in less than a second. The mountain took your life, and with it all your/our dreams. Yet all will somehow remain.

'You were the most wonderful person I have ever met. Thank you for letting me spend together your final moments on this planet.

'I would give anything for this to have happened to me rather than you. Lykke til up there.'

Robsahm was a semi-professional runner, also working as a chemistry teacher in Oslo.

She finished fourth in the Short Trail World Championships in 2025, and was regarded as a hot prospect in the sport.

Her family told local media: 'In the midst of the deep sorrow over the loss of Ida, we would like to extend a warm thank you to the running community.

'Ida was a big part of the community, and all the care and consideration in this cruel situation means a lot.'

Her coach, Sindre Buraas, added: 'It came as a shock. You can't deal with it right away. 'She was in a place in a terrain and an environment where she had been so much, so comfortable.

Benitez said: 'I would give anything for this to have happened to me rather than you'

'She was torn away from us and from her life. It leaves deep traces. It is bottomlessly sad in every way.

'I would like to highlight Ida as a fantastic athlete. A person with a big heart for the people around her and for the sport, and the project we had together, which was to run as fast as possible.

'A very good athlete and a very nice person to work with, who I have bonded very closely with and had daily conversations with.'

Sports.title: Paul Gascoigne reveals why he knew Tottenham 'were going to struggle'... as his old club slump to bottom of the Premier League before the international break
Sports.content:
Former Tottenham midfielder Paul Gascoigne has pinpointed the moment he knew Spurs would struggle this season.

The north London side have endured a nightmare start to their first full season under Roberto De Zerbi as they sit at the foot of the table without a win in five Premier League games.

Despite finishing 17th in back-to-back seasons, the Lilywhites – who spent over £300million on a rebuild in the summer – have hit a new low, with just two points from a possible 15, their worst-ever start to a top-flight campaign.

Spurs' struggles have been a surprise to many due to the heaps of business they did in the summer transfer window. However, Gascoigne, who played over 100 times in white, is not so shocked.

'Last season was incredible,' Gascoigne told talkSPORT. 'I went to their training ground; it was unbelievable. And straight away in my head, I thought, "They are going to struggle".

'Because everything is on a plate for them; when I played, the stuff and equipment we had. Everything is on a plate for them, but they have got to buck their ideas up.

Former Spurs midfielder Paul Gascoigne has said he expected Tottenham to struggle this season

The Lilywhites are rock bottom of the Premier League after the first five games of the campaign

Gascoigne says stars have 'everything on a plate' and don't have to fight

'The fans were fantastic when I was there, so they've got to do better this season.'

Tottenham's torrid start is already taking its toll on De Zerbi, and following the third defeat of the season against Villa, he could not hide his emotions.

He hit out at his team’s defensive ‘fragility’ and the feeble manner of Villa’s goals, especially the ‘unacceptable’ second, scored on the break by Nicolas Jackson at the start of the second half.

'I was very disappointed, very sad, very frustrated with the performance,' fumed De Zerbi. 'We can’t lose this game in this way, absolutely. We can’t concede the second goal. We can’t lose balance.

'At the beginning of the second half I spoke with the four attackers, to use their heads, be calm. It was minute 51. All the second half, be calm, play, enjoy, don’t take risks. But the goal we conceded, the second goal, was incredible.'

De Zerbi was no happier about the opener, scored by Johan Manzambi when Spurs were down to ten men because Micky van de Ven was off having treatment for a facial cut after a clash of heads with Tyrone Mings.

'I don’t want to speak about the first half when we dominated and created more chances to score,' said De Zerbi. 'My focus is on why we concede the first goal with 10 players, just for one minute in that situation.

'We can stay stronger, we can communicate more, we can defend in a compact way. I put [Rodrigo] Bentancur to centre back and Mateus Fernandes into midfield. If we have a red card, we could play for 60 minutes with 10 players, so what is the problem?'

Sports.title: England's fastest bowler calls it quits: 97mph Mark Wood admits defeat after knee surgery and retires at 36 - ending his Ashes dream
Sports.content:
England's fastest bowler calls it quits: 97mph Mark Wood admits defeat after knee surgery and retires at 36 - ending his Ashes dream

Mark Wood, England’s fastest ever bowler, has announced his international retirement after finally admitting defeat in an injury battle of 18 months.

Wood, 36, played only once - the Ashes Test defeat in Perth last November - after breaking down with a left knee issue during the Champions Trophy in late February 2025.

He put himself through intensive rehabilitation to get fit for last winter’s Ashes, but it ended in anguish when his body reacted badly to him bowling at close to maximum speed in the first innings of the eight-wicket loss to Australia.

It was his ability to produce 90mph pace without much in the way of build-up that persuaded England’s selectors to gamble on him against the Australians, throwing him into the first Test despite reporting discomfort in an internal practice match - but he managed just 11 overs and sported a knee brace post match.

Wood was ruled out of the 4-0 series drubbing on December 9, saying he was ‘gutted’ but it was not for the want of trying.

Now, having spent the summer trying to prolong his career under the guidance of knee consultant Simon Ball, he is calling time on a career that produced high-octane theatre on the international stage and 118 Test wickets at a cost of 31 runs each.

Mark Wood made his last Test appearance in the first Test at Perth last November

'When you speak to other people, they say it hits you in the face, there’s a big feeling around that being it, "you’re done",' he told Sky Sports.

'I’ve never really had that, I love playing cricket, I love playing for England, that’s been something I’ve felt really strongly about and proud to do. But I’ve had a lot of injuries.

'I’ve always found a way where I’ve believed I’d come back and had that resilience where I’m going to come back again, or I’ll be better, or I’ll prove somebody wrong again, but this time it’s just ground me down really.

'It’s been a long time since Perth, that was in November 2025 my last game, so it’s been a year and a half really where it’s just sort of ground me down to thinking I’m never going to get back to that level.

'Plus the contract situation. My contract ends in September, and I think it just feels like the right time.

'I never really wanted to give up England, but the lads that are coming through are doing a fantastic job and the news should be about the lads going to get their contracts and I can just focus on other things.'

A decision to have ‘tidy-up’ surgery in July appears to have been his last throw of the dice, after becoming frustrated with taking a patient approach to a return. ‘How long is a piece of string? It was improving, but slowly, slowly,’ he said, of his rehabilitation prior to undergoing the knife.

Wood was a member of England’s 2019 and 2022 World Cup-winning teams in 50-over and T20 cricket respectively, but it was as much for his 100 per cent commitment to bowling fast that makes him stand out from any other player of his generation.

Two years ago, he produced a delivery of 97.1mph against West Indies at Trent Bridge, while his average speed was 91.2mph - the highest recorded in a Test match on British soil.

The newly-retired Wood embraces one-day captain Harry Brook ahead of Tuesday's game against Sri Lanka at Chester-le-Street

Twelve months earlier, he was man of the match with seven wickets at Headingley as England defeated Australia to keep their hopes of an Ashes comeback alive.

Wood’s Test record against Australia, in fact, was better than his overall return and he was the visiting bowler that came out with the most credit from the 2021-22 Ashes when he claimed 17 scalps in four appearances. His hopes of reprising his role in next year's home series, though, are now over.

Hugely popular with supporters for his affable personality and fulsome heart, it is understood he is paying homage to his north-east roots by saying goodbye to the game at his home ground of Chester-le-Street on Tuesday, during England’s one-day series opener against Sri Lanka.

Wood’s central contract runs out next week and it is anticipated that he moves straight from dressing room to commentary box with a more regular role with Sky Sports, for whom he has worked on several occasions this summer.

England managing director Rob Key paid tribute to the departing Wood, saying: 'It’s been a privilege to watch the latter part of a great career.

'To have been a point of difference in Ashes series wins, a World Cup, and to have thrilled crowds every time he got the ball in his hand is something very few players achieve.

'He can look back with enormous pride on a career very well spent.'

Sports.title: The 'miracle doctor' and the Covid jab fraud Arsenal star: New questions are raised over Granit Xhaka's second vaccination as he faces a grilling and up to FIVE YEARS in jail
Sports.content:
The 'miracle doctor' and the Covid jab fraud Arsenal star: New questions are raised over Granit Xhaka's second vaccination as he faces a grilling and up to FIVE YEARS in jail

Fresh questions have emerged over the legitimacy of Granit Xhaka's Covid-19 vaccination certificate with a rapid turnaround between travelling to Switzerland and playing a Premier League match.

According to a report in Tages-Anzeiger, Xhaka's vaccine certificate – which Swiss authorities suspect to be forged – is dated November 11, 2022.

Yet just 24 hours later, Arsenal won 2-0 away at Wolves in the final game before the Qatar World Cup – a match Xhaka started but lasted only 16 minutes due to a gastrointestinal infection.

The Swiss national team captain is said to have 'obtained' the certificate from a family doctor in Lucerne, raising questions about whether Arsenal would have sanctioned foreign travel the day before a Premier League match.

Xhaka posted a team photo on Instagram on the date of his second vaccination, where he was presented with a framed shirt during training to mark his 200th Premier League appearance for Arsenal. He was also pictured training in London on that day.

Xhaka admitted wrongdoing yesterday, though his post stops short of a legal confession with the 33-year-old expected to be interviewed by Swiss authorities in due course. The offence carries a maximum prison sentence of five years.

Granit Xhaka is seen being substituted for Arsenal on November 12, 2022, the day after his disputed vaccine certificate is dated

In photos put out by his club he was also training with Arsenal in London on the day of the Swiss jab certificate date - November 11, 2022

Records show that Doctor Andrea Ludwig signed two vaccine certificates for Xhaka: January 25 2022 and November 11 2022

'In recent days, there has been much reporting about a matter from my past,' Xhaka said. 'I would like to address this personally.

'Regarding the Covid-19 vaccination, I was personally very uncertain and had serious concerns at the time. I felt deep distrust of the vaccine and was plagued by fear and uncertainty.

'In this turbulent emotional state, I obtained a vaccination certificate instead of clarifying my open questions through the proper channels. Today I clearly see that this was not the right course of action. It was a mistake. I am sorry.

'I take responsibility for this decision, am committed to investigating the matter, and am fully cooperating with the relevant authorities.'

Despite his admission, Swiss authorities reiterated to Daily Mail Sport that Xhaka is presumed innocent until proven guilty. The alleged doctor, Andrea Ludwig, maintains her innocence.

Doctor Ludwig has faced wider scrutiny over her conduct during the coronavirus pandemic. She was criticised for treating seriously ill coronavirus patients with cancer drug opaganib despite it never being an approved treatment – and was dubbed a 'miracle doctor' by sarcastic critics.

Xhaka posted this image from the training ground - the day of his apparent second vaccine

Xhaka is pictured with his wife Leonita, who has been with the footballer since 2015

On Monday, the Swiss authorities told Daily Mail Sport: 'We can confirm the Prosecutor's Office of the Canton of Lucerne has initiated a corresponding investigation against Granit Xhaka.

'The aim is to determine whether there is a behaviour that is legally relevant in connection with a possible forgery of a false notarisation or/and the falsification of documents.

'The person concerned is presumed innocent. The investigation is pending.'

Records show that Ludwig signed two vaccine certificates for Xhaka: January 25, 2022 and November 11, 2022.

The first was on the eve of Arsenal's training camp in the United Arab Emirates while the second was three days before he travelled to the Qatar World Cup.

Xhaka is not thought to have broken any laws regarding travelling to Qatar or Dubai, as vaccines were not compulsory.

Sunderland captain Xhaka is not joining up with Switzerland while he is under investigation

He is also not expected to face any repercussions in English football, as the FA or the Premier League did not mandate vaccines during the pandemic.

Due to the investigation, Xhaka has been axed from the Switzerland squad for their upcoming Nations League matches against North Macedonia, Scotland and Slovenia.

He holds their all-time appearance record with 152 games for the national team and most recently captained them to the World Cup quarter-finals in North America.

Ludwig justified the use of opaganib under 'compassionate use': the officially regulated use of drugs not yet approved outside of clinical trials.

According to news outlet 20 Minutes, a controlled study was unable to prove that the drug worked as a remedy for COVID despite Ludwig claiming that it was effective with individual patients.

Sports.title: Inside Andoni Iraola's Liverpool: Everything he's changed from the Arne Slot era behind the scenes, how he clamped down on team leaks, his private challenge to Alexander Isak and where he feels Reds can still improve
Sports.content:
Inside Andoni Iraola's Liverpool: Everything he's changed from the Arne Slot era behind the scenes, how he clamped down on team leaks, his private challenge to Alexander Isak and where he feels Reds can still improve

After most games, Andoni Iraola chooses not to speak to his players.

The Basque boss may appear calm but his mind is usually whirring, fuelled by adrenaline after 90 minutes of shouting instructions from the technical area.

So the squad are left in the dark, left to wonder whether they have impressed or not. Iraola will cool off, collect his thoughts and sleep on it before delivering a measured verdict, never getting too high or low.

Normally, it is the next afternoon that Iraola addresses his troops and debriefs them on the good, the bad and the ugly of their performances.

This time, the best part of a month will pass before the majority of Liverpool’s big-hitters are back at base.

An unprecedented three-week international window follows. Most club managers will tell you that although these ‘breaks’ may earn them a chance for a bit of autumnal sun, they are also periods spent stressing over tactical deficiencies and potential injuries.

Has Andoni Iraola seen the intensity, verve and exciting football he so craves from this Liverpool team? The answer is yes, but only in glimpses

Alexander Isak has started the season well, with four goals already in the Premier League. But Iraola wants more from his front man

Iraola and Co have plenty to mull over during the time off – though he is expected to spend some of it still working at the AXA Training Centre with those not on international duty. He will have a well-deserved rest, of course, but he is hardly heading on holiday for three weeks.

After seven games of his tenure, he has won four and drawn three. Iraola had made slow starts at all of his previous clubs – especially Bournemouth, where his nine-match winless run was well documented – so his first real month in situ represents a fair return.

But has he seen the intensity, verve and exciting football he so craves from this Liverpool team?

The answer is yes, but only in glimpses. Half an hour against Ipswich at Portman Road, an hour against Tottenham in the Carabao Cup, a comfortable win over Atletico Madrid.

Those high points are balanced out by an insipid draw with Fulham, and vulnerable afternoons against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest that could have ended in two defeats rather than two draws.

Iraola wants his team to suffocate their opposition like his Bournemouth side did. In this regard, Alexander Isak is key. The £125million man has started the season well: four goals in the Premier League including a brace at Ipswich and one at Bournemouth to help Liverpool to wins they might not have achieved last season.

But Iraola wants more from his front man. He craves a style that sees his team camped in the opposition half, not giving them a second's respite. His goal return has been pleasing but the boss will not be happy until he sees Isak morphing into a more complete forward.

‘Defending is an attacking weapon,’ said Isak in an interview with BBC Sport last week.

Iraola insists the demands on Isak are the same as anyone, be it a £125m player or an academy kid like Lewis Koumas, whom he has described as ‘contagious’. The Welshman clearly lacks Isak’s finishing instinct but more than makes up for it with his relentless off-the-ball running.

Days at Liverpool's AXA Training Centre have become a lot more on-pitch focused and Iraola is more hands-on than Slot, who would hold lots of meetings

Iraola has been impressed with young forward Lewis Koumas, particularly his off-the-ball work

Iraola does not treat Isak differently based on his price tag and has been unafraid to show him clips of rookie Koumas, who sets the gold standard for off-the-ball work.

On the other hand, Iraola has been demanding more of Koumas with the ball at his feet and the former Hull City loanee had several loose touches on Sunday that were noted.

Everyone, in the manager’s eyes, can improve and become more rounded – though he is aware each player has their own skillset.

Under 21s boss Rob Page, once of Wales, has been in regular contact with Iraola, who seems genuinely interested in the youngsters. ‘I knew the gaffer would love Koumas from the minute he stepped in,’ said Page last week.

In an ideal world, Iraola would switch at least two of his front three around the hour mark. He has told them he wants them to be ‘dead’ when they leave the pitch, allowing fresh legs – ‘finishers’ not substitutes – to take their place.

If Cody Gakpo and Bradley Barcola, say, have put in their shift, Iraola believes Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz – or any combination of the wide quartet – can come on and finish the job. No player is treated differently based on their price tag or status, remember.

Iraola wants Isak to lead the press with more ferocity, getting on the ball more, working better in tandem with Florian Wirtz.

Speaking of the German, Iraola also will spend the break considering his midfield puzzle. In the first fortnight of the season, it was a contentious issue as Liverpool were played through far too easily. Ryan Gravenberch has since paid for it by being replaced in the favoured XI.

Trey Nyoni is knocking on the door for a first Premier League start after impressing in cameos and other competitions

Due to midweek games, Iraola is getting nowhere near as much time on the training pitch as he would like

Alexis Mac Allister has shown his best form in well over a year but the issue is not resolved just yet. Iraola, for what it is worth, does not think his midfield conundrum is a personnel issue. He wants to play with one No 6, one No 8 and one No 10.

Often, all three of them want to be the No 10 and players have got in each other’s way.

In this regard, 19-year-old academy star Trey Nyoni is seriously knocking on the door for a first Premier League start after impressing in cameos and in other competitions.

Iraola likes Nyoni a lot and trusts in youth. It is why the club opted not to sign a midfielder in the last week of the transfer window when Lamine Camara of Monaco was offered around.

Had Wirtz not been a £116m signing whom Iraola was tasked with getting the most out of, the move might have already happened: Nyoni and Mac Allister at the heart of midfield, Dominik Szoboszlai as a No 10 with fewer defensive duties, a role in which the Hungarian thrives.

These are all issues that plagued Arne Slot and ultimately cost him his job.

Iraola, though, believes his side are improving every week and slowly getting to grips with his complex off-the-ball demands, including when to ‘jump’ forward and initiate pressing movements.

He is learning on the job and getting his ideas across is harder at Liverpool than Bournemouth because of one simple reason: they cannot train as much. Due to midweek games, Iraola is getting nowhere near as much time on the training pitch as he would like.

Days have become a lot more on-pitch focused and Iraola is more hands-on than Slot, who would hold lots of meetings. He appears to have buy-in from the dressing room, but so does every new manager who replaces one that failed.

Iraola's assistants Tommy Elphick (left) and Shaun Cooper (right) are said to be well-liked in the dressing room

The Basque will spend some of his international break mulling over how to get the best out of Florian Wirtz and solve his midfield muddle

It is about making early impressions stand the test of time and that will be Iraola’s next task. His English assistants, Tommy Elphick and Shaun Cooper, are said to be well-liked. Both are younger than the boss and perhaps connect better with the squad.

The trio, alongside Spaniard Pablo de la Torre, often have mini-meetings in their offices and the managerial team see themselves as ‘assistants to the players’ rather than authoritarian figures.

This fits in with Liverpool’s head coach model and, for this reason, Iraola has not been able to change too much from the Slot era – though there are some alterations. For example, training times are different, as are the ‘report’ times (when players are asked to arrive at the training ground). He adjusts the schedule based on the kick-off time of the next game.

Slot would often name his XI the day before the match, whereas Iraola does not tell players until a matter of hours before kick-off. It has put a halt to online team leaks which became all too common under the previous regime and were frustrating for many.

Former boss Slot chose to live away from the city to have a chance to switch off, whereas Iraola is living in Formby, where Jurgen Klopp resided. His main hobby is cycling – the wind mask and helmet have helped him go under cover during coastal rides.

Iraola’s two children already have their favourite player at Liverpool – though out of fairness to the whole squad, the boss will keep the individual a secret! – and his family is settling after the boss delayed his move up to allow the kids to finish the school year in Dorset.

In terms of his demeanour, Iraola is likeable and pleasant to deal with. So was Slot, to be fair, and Iraola will know being a nice guy gets you nowhere. He is always smiling and fiddling with a pen that has five different colours.

While some areas of the pitch have required the red pen treatment, one area that has been a major positive is defence, and in particular new signing Jeremy Jacquet.

The Frenchman has looked imperious, with a maturity way beyond his years.

He is only 21, remember, and barely had a pre-season due to a minor injury. He had not played for previous club Rennes from February onwards due to a shoulder problem and had, of course, never played in the Premier League until a month ago.

Noting all of those factors, Jacquet could have been forgiven for needing a bedding-in period but he has taken to his new surroundings with ease and appears a perfect partner for Virgil van Dijk, 14 years his senior.

The loss of Ibrahima Konate on a free transfer to Real Madrid felt like a hammer blow at the time but the topic has been forgotten thanks to Jacquet's impressive start.

New signing Jeremy Jacquet has made an impressive start to life in England. The 21-year-old has looked imperious, with a maturity way beyond his years

Ronald Araujo deserves praise, too. Iraola called the Uruguay international to sell him on the move to Liverpool and the Barcelona captain agreed to it immediately. Within 48 hours, the deal was done and he signed on loan. It is understood he is already hopeful of making the move permanent for a pre-agreed fee of £47.1m.

Giovanni Leoni is on the comeback trail and in the last stages of recovery after tearing his ACL on debut last September, while Conor Bradley is doing ball work for the first time since his nasty knee injury in January. Light at the end of a very long tunnel.

Left back Milos Kerkez has been criticised by fans and pundits alike but Iraola believes he is making strides and slowly becoming the player he was at Bournemouth before his big move to Liverpool in 2025.

So the defence feels settled, for now at least. The attackers all know where the goal is, too, but it is that all-important off-the-ball work that will buy them a golden ticket into Iraola’s good books. Intensity, intensity, intensity.

Sports.title: Lewis Hall reveals decision to snub Man United was a 'no-brainer' as Newcastle star opens up on transfer saga - with Michael Carrick in the hunt for a new left-back
Sports.content:
Newcastle and England defender Lewis Hall has revealed he didn't want to join Manchester United because of the vision presented to him by new Magpies boss Matthias Jaissle.

Hall, 22, was of strong interest to United in the summer as they searched for a left back, but the Red Devils opted to hold fire on any approach after Newcastle made it clear they didn't want to lose him.

But Hall wanted to stay on Tyneside too, and has detailed why he sees himself staying at the club for a number of years yet.

'No, honestly, it didn't (affect me),' he said of interest in his services. 'I guess whenever you're linked to another team, you know that you're doing something right. I guess it's just a credit to your own performances and how you are as a player, how you are as a person.

'I took that as a positive, but at the same time, I knew how much I love playing here and I knew that since the manager came in, I knew the ambitions and what we wanted to achieve.

'After not many conversations, not many training sessions, I knew that the manager was going to be really good for this club and I knew that as a team, bringing in new players and improving the squad was really important and as soon as we did that, it was a no-brainer really to sign.'

Lewis Hall has revealed he rejected Manchester United due to the project at Newcastle

Hall had been on Michael Carrick's radar with United in the hunt for a new left-back

Hall has just put pen to paper on a new deal at Newcastle and earned a recall into the England squad after missing out on a spot at the World Cup.

Newcastle have had a mixed start to the season, but Hall scored in the 2-1 win over Hull at the weekend, which moved the Magpies to ninth in the Premier League table.

'He's a top guy. He's been so good to me,' he said of new manager Jaissle. 'He gives me the licence to express myself as long as I do the defensive work and do the running that's required for this position, which is quite a lot of work.

'But I'm happy to do it as long as it benefits the team. He's been a positive for everyone who's come in so far.'

United, meanwhile, are keen on improving their defence next summer after buying in midfield this year.

They maintain an interest in Hall, but are believed to have assessed other options, including Brighton's Ferdi Kadioglu, Ian Maatsen of Aston Villa and Racing Santander's Jorge Salinas.

Sports.title: Football legend Lothar Matthaus, 65, parties at Oktoberfest with his 27-year-old girlfriend - who is younger than his two daughters, but who he insists will not become his SIXTH wife
Sports.content:
Germany legend Lothar Matthaus enjoyed Oktoberfest celebrations over the weekend – with his 27-year-old girlfriend who is younger than his daughters. The former Bayern Munich midfielder and Theresa Sommer enjoyed the 191st annual celebrations at Kafer Wiesn Schanke on the Theresienwiese in Munich, and posed for the cameras. The model, who is 38 years his junior, wore a traditional strapless, floor-length satin gown in a champagne tone and a fitted bodice, while Matthaus opted for a light blue waistcoat over a short-sleeve shirt in something close to traditional lederhosen. As a couple, Matthaus and Sommer have gained plenty of attention over the years, having seemingly dated for around 18 months and been first spotted together skiing in Austria in April last year. Matthaus's life off the pitch has seldom been quiet, with the former Germany captain going through five divorces. Matthaus married his first wife, Silvia, in 1981. The couple had two children – Alisa born in 1986 and Viola born in 1988 – but divorced in 1992. Football legend Lothar Matthaus (right), 65, posed with his 27-year-old girlfriend Theresa Sommer (left) at Oktoberfest The couple were first spotted together in spring last year, with the former midfielder insisting he does not plan on getting married for a sixth time In the same year, Lolita Morena gave birth to his third child, Loris. Matthaus and Morena, a Swiss model and TV presenter who represented her country at Miss World in 1982 and Miss Universe a year later, were married in 1994 but divorced in 1999 shortly before his retirement. He found love again in the Serbian capital in the shape of 31-year-old fashion entrepreneur Marijana Colic. She and Matthaus tied the knot in November 2003, but their marriage came to an end four years later after a lengthy divorce case in Salzburg – their last shared residence. The pair initially separated after Matthaus began dating Ukrainian model Kristina Liliana Chudinova in 2007. Colic, who still bears Matthaus's surname, filed for divorce soon afterwards. During the year-long divorce case, the couple allegedly looked to reach an out-of-court settlement over the division of their assets. The former Bayern Munich star reportedly offered his ex-wife an €100,000 settlement and the ownership of their penthouse in Budapest. While details of the divorce case were not made public, Blic reported Colic did not appeal the ruling, suggesting she was satisfied with the outcome. Matthaus married his first wife Sylvia in 1981 and divorced in 1992. The couple are pictured here with their second child Viola in 1990 He married TV presenter and Swiss model Lolita Morena (right) in 1994 Matthaus married his third wife, Marijana Colic, in 2003 but divorced in 2007 Matthaus then married Ukrainian model Kristina Liliana Chudinova in 2008 The Germany great's most recent divorce came in 2021, when he separated from his fifth wife, Anastasia Klimko By the time the divorce was officially ratified in January 2009, Matthaus had already married Chudinova. He was 47 at the time, 26 years older than her. The pair met at the Oktoberfest in Munich in 2007 and exchanged vows in Las Vegas in December 2008. The fact the pair tied the knot came as a surprise in itself, given they briefly went separate ways in February 2008 before reconciling their differences. Matthaus's fourth marriage hit the rocks early in 2010, when tabloids released pictures of his wife passionately embracing an unnamed Monaco business leader on his yacht during a holiday in Sardinia. Matthaus married for a fifth and hitherto last time in 2014, when he tied the knot with Anastasia Klimko, from whom he had a son, Milan. The couple divorced in 2021 but were spotted together at the Oktoberfest two years later, leading to speculation a rekindling of their flame may be on the cards before pictures with Sommer emerged. Matthaus and Sommer were in attendance as Ousmane Dembele was crowned winner of the men's Ballon d'Or last year, ahead of Barcelona starlet Lamine Yamal. That's when their relationship appeared to be confirmed. But there will be no marriage, according to the man himself. 'I definitely don't plan on getting married again,' he told reporters earlier this year.

Sports.title: Chelsea among top European clubs eyeing Gambian 15-year-old midfielder - and are weighing up stealing a march on the competition as he stars in U17 tournament
Sports.content:
Chelsea among top European clubs eyeing Gambian 15-year-old midfielder - and are weighing up stealing a march on the competition as he stars in U17 tournament

Chelsea are among a number of top European clubs tracking highly-rated Gambian teenager Adama Jeng.

The 6ft 2in midfielder, still only 15, has been impressing for Gambia's Under-17 national team at the WAFU Zone A U-17 tournament in Senegal.

Gambia, known as the Baby Scorpions, beat the hosts 5-3 on penalties to win the final on Monday.

Jeng, who turns 16 in December, is regarded as one of the most promising talents in African football and has been excelling in the holding midfield role.

He has come through the Samger FC academy, who have a proven track record of developing young talents for Europe.

The teenager's performances and potential have alerted Europe's top clubs who recognise he is one of the most talented midfielders in his age group.

Adama Jeng has attracted interest from several big clubs across Europe

Bayern Munich, Benfica, Sporting Lisbon and Paris FC along with Chelsea are all understood to have been monitoring Jeng's progress during the WAFU tournament in Dakar.

His suitors are expected to continue keeping tabs on the midfielder as they weigh up a move.

Chelsea are highly competitive in recruiting talent at that age group and see Jeng as a potential star in the making.

They are assessing whether to move swiftly to head off competition from their rivals with Monaco and Union Saint-Gilloise also in the running.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
