Sports.title: Wolff tried to help Masi ‘for the good of the sport, and for us’ in 2021 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff has revealed details of his conversations with former race director Michael Masi before his controversial call in the 2021 championship-decider.

Masi lost his job over his mishandling of the 2021 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix. He arranged a final-lap restart in contravention of the rules which led Wolff’s driver Lewis Hamilton to lose the championship to Max Verstappen.

Hamilton and Verstappen were involved in a series of controversial collisions over the course of 2021. Wolff, who previously called Masi “disrespectful” and a “liability”, said he had concerns over how the race director reacted to feedback from the drivers.

“I really tried to speak to Michael and guide him all along the year,” Wolff told High Performance. “I said ‘listen I’ve been in the sport for a long time, listen to the drivers, don’t always be stubborn in your decision making, don’t be arrogant’.”

Wolff admitted his motivation in speaking to the race director was partly to advance Mercedes’ interest.

“I tried that for the good of the sport, and obviously also for us as a team not to be vulnerable to situations that could be totally detrimental,” he said.

Masi contradicted the regulations and his past interpretation of them by arranging a final-lap restart at Yas Marina by removing the lapped cars between Hamilton and Verstappen, but not any of the others. The FIA later ruled this had been an error. Verstappen passed Hamilton immediately after the restart, clinching his first world championship and denying Hamilton a record-breaking eighth.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Wolff said Masi’s actions were “inexcusable.”

“You could say the empathy should make me realise how he feels,” he said. “I realise how it feels.

“And I know that’s not good, and bad, but he could have thought about it all year long, when people, not only me, tried to support him in the right way.

“So sometimes you have to just realise that someone is just doing his own thing or taking his own decisions. So for me, I don’t care about it anymore.”

However he admitted he still reflects on the lost championship “every week”.

“I mainly think about it because I think Lewis deserved to be the greatest of all time with eight world championship titles,” he said. “And you can argue all along about that year.

“I think Max and Lewis were deserving champions. There were instances during the year where Max lost some points that he shouldn’t have lost. You look at the crash in Monza both of them had. So both deserving champions, but on that particular afternoon in Abu Dhabi, it was unfair.”

Following his departure from F1, Masi joined SRO Motorsports Australia last week as head of sporting operations.

Sports.title: Poll: Should F1 change its rules to make Virtual Safety Car periods fairer? | Debates and Polls
Sports.content:
The outcome of last weekend’s Spanish Grand Prix was effectively decided by Lance Stroll’s retirement on lap 15.

The Virtual Safety Car was deployed while the Aston Martin driver parked up in a run-off area. It only lasted

seconds, but as far as Lando Norris was concerned its timing could not have been worse.

Norris was leading when the VSC period began seconds after he passed the pit lane entrance. Andrea Kimi Antonelli, second, was able to pit during the VSC period, gaining a useful advantage by pitting while the race was neutralised.

Every other driver on the track had the same opportunity to pit, with one exception: Norris. The VSC period ended moments before he reached the pit lane entrance.

Afterwards Norris expressed frustration that the race’s only VSC period was timed in such a way that it gave everyone apart from him a chance to make a low-cost pit stop. While it’s certainly the case he was unlucky, should F1 try to prevent a similar situation happening again?

The Virtual Safety Car problem

In F1, like other series such as IndyCar, Safety Car periods can often have a disruptive effect on drivers’ strategies. They may occur at a more advantageous time for some drivers than others (as was the case when Norris scored his first win in Miami two years ago).

However the Virtual Safety Car, which F1 introduced in 2015, created a new kind of problem. During a classic Safety Car period, every driver has the opportunity to make a pit stop. But as a VSC period can be much shorter, it is possible that only some drivers may have the chance to pit.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

This is more likely to happen in certain circumstances. For example, when the track is very long, or if conditions are wet creating longer lap times, or when the field is tightly compressed after a start or restart.

There have only been a few cases of drivers being unable to pit during a VSC period since the rules were introduced. One notable example occured in the 2024 Brazilian Grand Prix, where all but four drivers were able to pit during a VSC period.

Possible solutions

No change

The striking thing about Norris’s misfortune on Sunday was how unusual it is. As these situations are so rare, it is not worth creating special rules to deal with them, which would create further complexity and scope for unintended consequences.

Introduce a minimum duration for VSC periods

It is unusual for VSC periods to last less than a lap in duration. When they do, it is usually only by a few seconds. Introducing a minimum length for VSC periods would ensure no driver suffers the same misfortune as Norris but make little difference to the majority of VSC deployments.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Forbid tyre changes during VSC periods

Other series which have similar mandatory tyre change rules to F1 do not allow drivers to fulfil the requirement to change tyres during a VSC period. This is the case in Formula 2, and F1 could simply adopt the same rule. Closing the pit lane entrance during a VSC period would have the same effect, though this would prevent drivers pitting for damage repairs or other reasons.

Introduce a lower pit lane speed limit during VSC periods

Drivers are able to gain an advantage by pitting during a VSC period because the speed of the cars on track is reduced while the pit lane speed limit stays the same. Reducing the pit lane speed limit could address this, though it would have to be very low, especially at tracks where the lower 60kph speed limit is used by default, and imposing it on cars in the pit lane when the VSC is deployed could be complicated.

Abolish the Virtual Safety Car

Revert to using the classic Safety Car for all interruptions to the race. This would likely result in longer disruptions to races and compress the field more frequently.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

I say

I find the VSC preferable to the regular Safety Car because it does a better job of preserving the competition as it stands, and not significantly altering the gaps between cars. It is unfortunate that in some, limited circumstances, it does create the possibility for some drivers to suffer a significant disadvantage. Introducing a minimum duration for VSC periods would seem the easiest and fairest way to tackle the problem, which is unlikely to add significant extra delays or cause knock-on problems.

Sports.title: Has Canelo Alvarez Declined Too Far for Christian Mbilli?
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez’s decline did not begin with Terence Crawford. Crawford removed the remaining doubt after Jaime Munguia, Edgar Berlanga and William Scull demonstrated that Canelo was losing the speed, activity and aggression that separated him from ordinary champions.

Those opponents suited Canelo, yet none fell before the final bell. He fought in brief spurts, leaned on single power punches and allowed long stretches to pass without forcing the action. His last stoppage occurred against Caleb Plant in November 2021.

The deterioration shows clearly in Canelo’s jab. During peak campaigns against Gennadiy Golovkin and Callum Smith, he drove an authoritative lead hand to dictate distance, split high guards and create openings for hooks. That punch has deteriorated into a lazy pawing motion that opponents parry with little concern.

Without an authoritative jab collecting a toll at the perimeter, aggressive opponents march straight into pocket range. That grants Christian Mbilli direct access to unload combinations without having to solve a layered defense first.

Canelo’s multi-punch body combinations vanished as well. The classic left hook downstairs doubled with a hook upstairs demanded explosive torque from his hips. He now settles for isolated overhand rights and looping hooks. Opponents brace for those solitary attempts and fire back before Canelo reorganizes his guard.

Scull exposed another troubling pattern. Once the Cuban gained confidence and let his hands go, Canelo spent long stretches parked against the ropes. That was not the slick baiting technique Canelo displayed in his prime.

A younger Canelo rested dynamically through trunk movement while keeping his base centered. The current version retreats straight back, physically resting his weight on the cables to catch his breath. That passive posture hands opponents ring generalship, influences judges, and gives away rounds on sheer inactivity.

Crawford dismantled those exact tendencies. Canelo chased him flat-footed in straight lines, loaded up on telegraphed blows and lacked the sustained output needed to flip the narrative. An elbow ailment provides an easy excuse, but that physical issue fails to explain the missing fire against Munguia, Berlanga and Scull.

Working alongside Oleksandr Usyk brings plenty of promotional chatter. Usyk provides tactical insights and conditioning drills, yet he cannot turn back the clock on Canelo’s legs or reflexes. Canelo started fighting professionally as a teenager in 2005. Over twenty years of prize fights, hard gym wars and brutal training have ground down his joints, leaving wear on his shoulders, knees and arms that no single training camp can scrub away.

Mbilli’s relentless tempo presents severe danger. The contender attacks in waves, pounding the torso, arms and shoulders when clean head openings close up. An aging veteran hunting for breathers between thirty-second charges struggles when confronted by someone who ignores the referee’s breaks and pushes the pace.

Canelo retains the superior boxing brain, but Mbilli meets him when the physical engine can no longer execute those master plans over twelve exhausting rounds. Spending over twelve months on the shelf following joint surgery rarely produces a fountain of youth. It often produces a slower fighter burdened with ring rust and relying on lucky one-shot counters. The debate no longer centers on how prime Canelo handled crude swarmers. The issue is how little of that elite operator walks into the ring tonight.

Canelo built his entire hall of fame run on intimidating guys into low-output chess matches. When opponents feared the return fire, they stayed on the outside, threw tentative jabs, and let Canelo dictate a glacial pace where his limited gas tank never became a liability. He could sit in neutral for two minutes of every round because thirty seconds of explosive, flashy counter combinations were enough to bank the frame on the cards.

Mbilli completely breaks that formula. He is the ultimate volume merchant. He does not possess top-shelf technical defense, but he does not care to. He enters the pocket like a bowling ball, throws 70 to 80 punches a round, and beats fighters around the collarbones, biceps, and ribcage until their guard drops from sheer exhaustion.

If Canelo cannot make Mbilli taste severe, concussive power in the opening three rounds, he is in for a horrific night. Without blazing hand speed, Canelo’s single-shot counters will bounce off Mbilli’s forehead while the Frenchman keeps driving forward.

Once Canelo gets forced into the ropes, the fight transforms from a technical boxing match into an attritional brawl. An aging fighter with twenty years of wear, a surgically repaired elbow, and a shallow engine cannot survive being battered along the cables for twelve continuous rounds. If Canelo spends the second half of the fight covering up in a high shell while Mbilli unloads hooks to his sides, the referee or the corner will be forced to save him from a punishing beating.

Sports.title: Jaime Munguía Ordered Into Bektemir Melikuziev Defense
Sports.content:
Jaime Munguía faces a mandatory defense that carries serious danger. The WBA ordered its super middleweight champion to negotiate with Bektemir Melikuziev, giving both camps until October 21 to reach an agreement.

Munguía spent years benefiting from calculated matchmaking. The clearest exception came against Canelo Alvarez, who dropped him and coasted to a wide decision in May 2024. Melikuziev lacks Canelo’s complete skillset, but his southpaw power and vicious body punching present an unusually severe threat.

“The WBA orders negotiations between Jaime Munguía and Bektemir Melikuziev for the super middleweight championship. They have until October 21 to reach an agreement,” said ESPN’s Salvador Rodriguez about the WBA’s order.

Failure to agree before the deadline will force the sanctioning body to send the bout to a purse bid.

Munguía (46-2, 35 KOs) captured the belt by outworking Jose Armando Resendiz over twelve rounds on May 2. He controlled that bout with sheer punch output, but Resendiz lacked the speed or punching power to make him pay for his customary defensive holes.

Bruno Surace revealed the real cost of those habits. The French underdog detonated a single overhand right to flatten Munguía in round six during their December 2024 meeting in Tijuana. Surace entered that ring with only five career knockouts.

Munguía avenged that defeat on points five months later in Saudi Arabia, but going twelve rounds did nothing to erase the technical carelessness that got him dropped. If an unproven puncher like Surace can connect so cleanly, Melikuziev can do considerably worse.

Melikuziev (17-1, 11 KOs) attacks with heavy hands and relentless intent downstairs. The 2016 Olympic silver medalist hunts from a southpaw stance, waiting for opponents to overcommit before uncorking his straight left hand.

That punch serves as the ultimate weapon against Munguía. The Tijuana native habitually drops his lead shoulder, flaring his elbows wide as he charges inside with looping rights. His guard splits apart, presenting an inviting path straight down the pipe. Canelo exploited that exact opening, splitting Munguía’s gloves with a short counter uppercut to put him on the canvas.

Munguía holds advantages in height and reach, yet physical dimensions offer little protection if he ditches his jab to brawl inside. Melikuziev relishes opponents who plant their feet in front of him. He ducks under wild punches, gains dominant foot position, and digs crunching hooks into the ribcage. Munguía’s smartest path requires pumping a stiff jab from range while refusing to get drawn into mid-ring fire fights. That approach demands strict round-by-round composure, a quality Munguía rarely maintains. His first reaction to taking a punch is always firing back with wild, prolonged flurries.

Melikuziev carries his own flaws. Gabriel Rosado knocked him unconscious with a single counter right hand in 2021 by timing his reckless forward rushes. Munguía throws the necessary volume to exploit that vulnerability, but trading on the inside turns the bout into an outright chin contest.

The WBA ruling presents an awkward problem for Golden Boy Promotions. Oscar De La Hoya relies on Munguía to headline cards and generate box office revenue. Melikuziev remains a high-risk stablemate who brings minimal commercial upside. Pitting them against each other risks derailing a major asset. Munguía could drop the belt and chase a softer payday. Vacating the title immediately after beating Resendiz would only validate complaints about his protected matchmaking.

Accepting the Melikuziev bout forces him to defend his belt against the exact puncher his career architecture was built to dodge.

Panic is the only realistic word for what Fernando Beltran and Oscar De La Hoya are experiencing right now. This WBA order is an operational disaster for Zanfer and Golden Boy because it blows up the entire business model they built around Munguía.

The belt was supposed to improve Munguía’s bargaining power, not force him into a low-paying fight with perhaps the most dangerous opponent available. Golden Boy finally rebuilt Munguía after the Canelo and Bruno Surace losses, secured a title against a manageable champion, and positioned him for another major event. Now the WBA is demanding a defense against a powerful southpaw who can attack every defensive flaw Munguía still has.

Golden Boy’s initial maneuver will likely involve offering Melikuziev step-aside compensation to clear the path. Promoting both fighters gives Oscar De La Hoya room to guarantee the Uzbek a showcase slot, a substantial fee, and a promised title shot down the road. That arrangement would buy Munguía time to hunt down a far more profitable voluntary defense while keeping his belt intact.

The October 21 deadline offers plenty of room to stall. Munguía’s team can easily drag out talks over financial splits, site locations, or distribution rights before asking for an extension. The WBA already let Rolando Romero bypass Shakhram Giyasov without rushing to a purse bid, handing Munguía’s side a proven playbook to drag their feet and test the sanctioning body’s resolve.

Dropping the title remains the ultimate eject button. Munguía could announce that lucrative opportunities elsewhere require his attention, but surrendering the belt without a single defense exposes the farce of taking it from Reséndiz in the first place. The hardware served its purpose when it promised leverage for major paydays. Melikuziev now forces Munguía to prove whether keeping that belt is worth risking his career against a genuine puncher.

Sports.title: Michael Spinks Denies Larry Holmes His Marciano Moment
Sports.content:
Michael Spinks shattered Larry Holmes’ pursuit of boxing history on September 21, 1985, taking a 15 round unanimous decision at the outdoor arena of the Riviera Hotel and Casino in Las Vegas.

Holmes (48-0, 34 KOs) entered the ring needing one victory to match Rocky Marciano’s iconic 49-0 mark. Another successful title defense would equal Joe Louis’ division benchmark of 20 consecutive defenses. The 35-year-old champion walked into the ring as a 6-1 favorite against a challenger moving straight up from the 175-pound ranks.

Spinks (27-0, 19 KOs) had unified the light heavyweight division, yet history stood firmly against him. Predecessors Archie Moore, Billy Conn and Bob Foster had all tried and failed to conquer reigning heavyweight kings. Spinks tipped the scales at a lean, conditioned 200 pounds after completing an intensive program under conditioning specialist Mackie Shilstone. That regimen relied on track sprints, resistance work, and targeted caloric intake.

The conditioning strategy paid off instantly. Rather than transforming into a traditional heavyweight slugger, he transported light heavyweight agility into the sport’s biggest division.

Holmes established control in rounds one and two through his signature left jab, but Spinks quickly dismantled that timing. The challenger utilized sudden lateral dips, unpredictable head slips, and varied foot angles to vacate the center line. Holmes soon found himself pawing with the lead hand rather than snapping the punishing, rhythmic jab that carried his long title reign.

Spinks exaggerated the champion’s hesitation by constantly switching directions and firing counters from unorthodox stances. His looping overhand right came over Holmes’ habitually low lead guard. Though the blow lacked true concussive force to stagger the heavyweight champion, the persistent threat forced Holmes to freeze after jabbing instead of letting combinations fly.

The second half of the bout produced a classic scoring issue. Holmes pressed forward and scored with the heavier singular wallops, but chasing Spinks proved far different from trapping him. Holmes struggled to cut the ring off cleanly, allowing the challenger to fire quick bursts and escape along the ropes.

Spinks exploited the optics of those sequences perfectly. In the closing thirty seconds of tight frames, the challenger launched quick flurries across Holmes’ guard, shoulders and face before skipping outside. Many blows landed on leather, yet the sheer flurry gave ringside officials eye-catching closing activity.

Holmes spent the final rounds hunting for an equalizer. Lingering back trouble surely restricted his mobility, but the mental burden of chasing Marciano’s ghost also took a toll. When Spinks refused to crumble during early skirmishes, Holmes cast aside the methodical rhythm that had grounded his championship dominance.

CompuBox numbers supported the challenger’s work rate, recording 318 landed shots out of 697 attempts for Spinks, against 248 of 567 for Holmes. Neither fighter suffered serious physical trauma over the 45 minutes of action.

Judges Harold Lederman and Dave Moretti turned in cards of 143-142, while Lawrence Wallace submitted a 145-142 tally, awarding Spinks the unanimous decision. Lederman noted that his scorecard sat deadlocked through fourteen rounds, with Spinks sealing the victory by outworking the champion in the final three minutes.

The loss hit Holmes hard, and the bitter aftermath carried over to the post-fight press gathering.

“I’m 35 fighting young men, and Rocky was 25 fighting old men. To be technical, Rocky couldn’t carry my jockstrap.”

Holmes later apologized for the remark. Spinks edged Holmes again via split decision seven months down the road, yet this initial Las Vegas clash holds lasting historical importance. Spinks demonstrated that an undersized champion did not require brute force to topple a giant. Precise conditioning, persistent lateral angles, and unrelenting activity were enough to pull an elite heavyweight completely out of his comfort zone. Holmes was carrying years of accumulated resentment that finally boiled over that night in Las Vegas.

The outburst had very little to do with Michael Spinks as an individual and almost everything to do with Holmes feeling chronically disrespected throughout his entire championship reign.

First, Holmes spent seven years reigning in the inescapable shadow of Muhammad Ali. When Holmes dominated a faded Ali in 1980, the public never truly forgave him for beating their icon. Instead of receiving unconditional praise as an all-time great heavyweight, Holmes routinely faced lukewarm crowds, critical press, and constant comparisons to fighters from past eras. He felt he had carried the heavyweight division with absolute professionalism without ever receiving the adoration given to Ali or Joe Frazier.

Second, the Marciano obsession amplified that frustration tenfold. Leading into the Spinks bout, the media spotlight fixated almost entirely on Rocky Marciano’s 49-0 mark rather than Holmes’ own historic accomplishments. Marciano’s family and older sports columnists openly rooted for Holmes to lose so the record would stay untouched. To Holmes, the comparisons felt inherently unfair. He saw himself as an active champion taking on prime contenders while Marciano had built his late record against aging legends like Joe Louis, Jersey Joe Walcott, and Ezzard Charles. When the decision went against him, that perceived injustice exploded into the infamous jockstrap remark.

Third, Holmes genuinely believed he won the fight. In his mind, he had walked Spinks down, landed the heavier and more damaging punches, and dictated ring position for fifteen rounds. To lose his heavyweight title, his unblemished record, and his historic milestone on a controversial decision based on what he considered slapping flurries felt like outright theft.

Rather than processing the setback in private, Holmes walked into the press room exhausted, injured, and deeply wounded by the sudden collapse of his historical quest. The irony, as you noted, was immediate: had he shown grace in defeat, the boxing public likely would have rallied around him for dropping a razor-thin decision at age thirty-five. By lashing out at Marciano, he instantly turned public sentiment against himself and alienated the very fans who were ready to appreciate his career.

When you watch the tape without audio or crowd influence, Holmes undeniably delivered the heavier, more authoritative blows. His right hands snapped Spinks’ head back, while many of Spinks’ combinations bounced harmlessly off Holmes’ high guard, forearms, or shoulders.

In traditional championship boxing scoring, effective aggression and clean, hard punching are supposed to carry the round. Holmes was the man moving forward, controlling center ring, and delivering the thudding shots that looked like actual heavyweight punches. The wire services saw it that way too, which is why the Associated Press and United Press International both scored the fight for Holmes.

Where Holmes ran into trouble with the ringside judges was purely optic. By following Spinks without cutting the ring off, he let Spinks dictate the visual tempo. When Spinks threw a four-punch flurry in the final twenty seconds of a round, even if three hit gloves, it created the illusion of dominance right as the bell rang. The judges rewarded that busy, awkward hustle over Holmes’ patient, single-punch stalking.

Losing a world championship on shoe-shine flurries when you landed the only hard shots of the night is enough to make any champion see red. It explains entirely why Holmes was so raw at the microphone afterward, convinced he had been robbed of Marciano’s milestone by judges who favored activity over real damage.

Sports.title: Pitbull Cruz Says He’s Willing To Fight Ryan Garcia
Sports.content:
San Diego, California – Saturday night at the Pechanga Arena, Isaac “Pitbull”Cruz (29-3-2, 19 KOs) successfully defended his WBC interim super lightweight title against Nestor Bravo (24-2, 17 KOs) in an ugly fight where referee Thomas Taylor had to intervene several times to put Bravo in line to stop him from roughing up Pitbull.

Taylor gave Bravo several warnings along with a point deduction in rounds 2 and 4 to stop him from holding, shoving, and even body-slamming Isaac to the ground. Nestor also landed a few low blows that appeared intentional. He appeared unable to handle Cruz’s pressure, looking overwhelmed and unable to stop the onslaught. When he finally appeared to have settled down in round six, Pitbull landed a clean left hook that sent Bravo to the canvas for the full 10-count.

After the fight, Nestor said what made Cruz such a difficult opponent was his awkwardness and his small size. He said Pitbull was not necessarily strong but hurt him with punches he didn’t see coming due to his awkward style. Before the fight, Ryan Garcia made his prediction via X by posting that he didn’t think Pitbull would defeat Bravo.

Then, once Pitbull won, he made another post: “Bravo Pitbull proved me wrong tonight. Let’s do this in December; the offer is on the table. I can tame a lion; I’m not to concerned about taming a pitbull.”

This began a series of posts whereby Ryan made it known his seriousness for wanting the fight and that if the fight is not accepted by Cruz this time around, he won’t entertain in the future.

Isaac told the media after the press conference he wants the fight and is not afraid to move up to welterweight, “Here I am for the challenge, and I am more than ready. Whether that be December, May, or September, I don’t care about the date. The desire is there, and we will do it.” For those present at the Pechanga arena, you could feel the energy of the fans chanting Pitbull and barking for Cruz. He became a household name after being one of the few fighters to go the distance with Gervonta Davis.

Since then, he’s only become a bigger star. Recently, he joined the Eddie Reynoso camp, which holds some of the elite Mexican boxers in the sport today: fighters Rafael Espinoza, Jaime Munguia, and former undisputed supermiddleweight champion Canelo Alvarez. He’s learning not only about boxing inside the ring but outside of it as well, as he wishes to create a legacy with a superstar profile among the great Mexican fighters of all time.

Sports.title: Lorenzo “Truck” Simpson Wins WBA Intercontinental Light Heavyweight Title
Sports.content:
On Saturday night, September 19th, in the co-main event of the Skyy Myles Promotions event entitled ‘The Supper,’ Lorenzo “Truck” Simpson defeated Shawn McCalman (17-3, 8 KOs) and won the WBA Intercontinental Title.

Going into the fight, the matchup was considered to be a 50/50 bout between two hungry boxers. Winning the vacant title was important to both boxers because it’s a regional belt that provides a boost in the rankings.

In the opening round of the southpaw vs. southpaw bout, McCalman got off to a good start as he was changing levels with an active jab. Simpson put his jab on display in the second round as he landed multiple jabs to the body.

The third round saw Simpson have success in regards to closing the distance and landing the left hand. As the round was coming to a close, McCalman connected with a few body shots.

The fourth round was highlighted by a solid uppercut landed by Simpson. In the fifth round, McCalman upped his production as he got back to working the jab and targeting the body.

The majority of the second half of the bout was fought in close quarters, as the back-and-forth match went the distance.

At the conclusion of the fight, the judges had to determine if they were swayed by McCalman’s volume or Simpson’s sharp power shots.

In a very technical fight, one judge scored the bout (96-94) in favor of Shawn McCalman. However, that judge’s scorecard was overruled by the other two judges, who both scored the fight (97-93) in favor of Lorenzo Simpson.

With the victory, Lorenzo “Truck” Simpson (17-3, 10 KOs) has won a title belt, and now he feels the sky is the limit. Next on his agenda is a bout against a boxer in the top 15.

Back in January 2017, Coach Calvin Ford and Coach Kenny Ellis were in the corner when Gervonta “Tank” Davis won his first world title. Now the question is, will Lorenzo “Truck” Simpson be the next world champion to come out of the Upton Boxing Center?

Sports.title: Keith Connolly Pitches Benn-Eubank Rubber Match at 168
Sports.content:
Conor Benn choosing to leap straight from a second-round knockout loss to Ryan into a third clash against Chris Eubank Jr. at 168 pounds looks like a cash grab rather than a legitimate sporting return. Rushing into another stadium payday before the UK rivalry expires takes precedence over sensible career preservation.

The condition of Benn’s chin demands serious scrutiny after Ryan stunned him inside three minutes and finished the job at 1:25 of round two. Throwing Benn back in the ring against an established, bigger operator after a brief break represents hazardous management. Benn already absorbed punishing artillery over twenty-four rounds during their initial two bouts.

“One hundred percent. 168 pounds, no excuses. The trilogy, another stadium fight, it’ll sell out. It’ll be a tremendous event, and then there’ll be no excuses. There’ll be a winner of the one-one series between the two guys. I expect it to happen. I think it’ll make the event big. Eddie Hearn with Chris Eubank. Myself and Dana White on one side backing Conor,” said manager Keith Connolly to talkSPORT Boxing.

That soundbite benefits Eubank far more than it helps Benn. Eubank escapes the brutal boils down to lower limits and enters the ring fully fueled. Benn piling on weight up to 178.4 pounds on fight night against Ryan merely demonstrated quick fluid retention, not the ability to trade functional super middleweight muscle against a seasoned campaigner.

Carrying sluggish pounds strips away Benn’s hand speed, the single attribute that gave the older man problems. Eubank gains total freedom to march forward, walk through incoming fire, and punish Benn in the pocket without the sapping weight restrictions that limited his output in the past.

The promotional split presents an aggressive battle behind the scenes. Connolly and Dana White would back Benn, with Eddie Hearn positioned in Eubank’s corner. Hearn spent years guiding Benn’s career. Hearn knows his former fighter’s technical deficiencies, stamina thresholds, and gym habits better than anyone else in the sport.

A standard recovery program would keep Benn out of heavy sparring, followed by a controlled confidence builder. Fast-tracking the trilogy brings immense gate receipts while Benn’s marketability remains intact. His management clearly prefers mining this family feud for quick millions rather than risking him against dangerous welterweights.

Eubank secures every physical edge at 168 pounds. Benn assumes all the medical hazards, trading his future punch resistance for one last massive stadium check.

Without Riyadh Season writing blank checks, the math completely falls apart. The first two encounters only happened because Saudi money absorbed the astronomical purses, underwriting the inflated demands of both camps while keeping pay-per-view prices low. Traditional broadcast economics cannot support those figures. If the Saudis decide they have zero interest in funding a third run between two damaged fighters, no standard commercial outfit can bridge the financial void.

DAZN, Boxxer, or Sky Sports operating on standard balance sheets cannot cut ten-million-dollar checks to men coming off definitive stoppage losses. Staging a stadium event at Wembley or Tottenham Hotspur Stadium costs millions just to open the turnstiles and turn on the lights. Gate receipts and a standard UK pay-per-view split would force both men to take a massive haircut from their previous paydays. When reality hits the accountants, the money will dry up fast.

Calling it a celebrity match between nepo babies accurately identifies the true product. Stripped of elite competitive relevance, this pairing relies solely on the nostalgia of their fathers’ names. Ryan exposed Benn inside four minutes as an undersized, one-dimensional slugger with a fragile chin. Eubank has drifted for years without winning a legitimate world title, relying on domestic drama rather than championship credentials.

Neither fighter commands global pay-per-view numbers outside the British market. Without international interest, the fight turns into a regional cash grab. If Dana White and Zuffa step in to foot the bill, they will quickly discover that UK nostalgia does not move subscription needles in North America. When the Saudi money train bypasses the station, both fighters will either take a fraction of their past purses or realize their lucrative family drama has priced itself out of the market.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Makes Zuffa Signing Look Worse
Sports.content:
Zuffa believed it landed pure royalty by securing Shakur Stevenson following his victory against Teofimo Lopez. The subsequent months delivered zero ring appearances, endless social media bickering, alongside an obstinate champion insisting on tailor-made parameters before stepping into the ring.

A lack of signed contracts triggered sharp public reaction.

“Zuffa have to really regret that Shakur Stevenson signing. All he has done is ruin his goodwill with the fans online and continue to be a pain in the ass to get a fight done for,” Tolboof posted on X.

The critique holds immense weight given the presence of ready internal rivals. José Valenzuela threw down an explicit challenge, handing the promotion an explosive pairing of roster talent. Stevenson discarded the possibility entirely.

Rayo delivers relentless offense, legitimate stopping power, plus an eagerness to trade in the pocket. Such an opponent forces Stevenson out of his safety zones, giving the promotional hierarchy a genuine look at their prize asset under fire. Ernesto Mercado offers another devastating threat capable of delivering the carnage Turki Alalshikh expects from these venture millions.

Stevenson ignores those dangerous tests. He spent valuable calendar time chasing Devin Haney at a catchweight limit of 144 pounds, demanding artificial terms against a larger rival. Haney relies on safety-first positioning, backfoot movement, minimal inside engagement. The brass faced grueling backroom wrangling merely to stage a bloodless fencing match devoid of crowd drama.

A collaborative company asset jumps at the Rayo encounter, establishing a fierce homegrown rivalry under the promotional banner. Stevenson prioritized stagnation, fixating on comfortable terms instead of stepping through the ropes.

Pure technical craft is obvious. The actual headache centers on functional execution for the brand. The Riyadh connection thrives on reckless courage, volatility, combatants chasing knockouts against devastating hitters. Stevenson brings retreat-first tactics, endless contract stalling, vast stretches of inactivity.

The brass presented him as their crown jewel. Stevenson spent his entire tenure turning that blockbuster signing into an overpriced promotional nightmare.

Dana White has to be feeling serious buyer’s remorse, even if he will never admit it publicly. White built his entire empire on a matchmaking philosophy that is the exact polar opposite of how Shakur Stevenson operates. In the UFC model, fighters take the hardest fights presented, stay active, and entertain the crowd. Stevenson brings the complete antithesis: high financial demands, a fence-and-retreat style that empties arenas, and an obsession with handpicking circumstances down to the exact pound.

Zuffa shelled out eight figures to make Stevenson a headline acquisition, expecting him to anchor major events. Instead, the promotion bought into months of dead air, endless social media bickering, and outright refusal to engage in in-house tests. Turning down José “Rayo” Valenzuela right out of the gate showed where Stevenson’s priorities sit. Rayo is a dangerous, aggressive hitter within the same organizational family who would have forced a firefight and given the fans real drama. Passing on that test while chasing a 144-pound handicap against Devin Haney proves Stevenson wants the safety of selective terms rather than testing himself against true offensive threats.

That calculated businessman approach is poison for a fledgling promotional brand trying to build genuine momentum. Matchmaking a risk-averse defensive specialist is difficult enough; matchmaking one who demands king’s ransom money while rejecting live punchers is an outright headache. When an elite technician refuses to take risks in the ring or at the negotiating table, the company is left paying millions just to watch its marquee investment gather dust on the shelf.

Triggering an escape clause in the contract would be the quickest way to end the bleeding, because keeping Shakur on the roster is a recipe for stagnation. If the Zuffa brass has a legal mechanism based on turned-down fight offers, inactivity periods, or failure to accept assigned dates, pulling that trigger makes absolute business sense.

The problem with holding onto a fighter like Shakur is the opportunity cost. Every month wasted trying to indulge his catchweight demands against Devin Haney is calendar space denied to fighters who actually want to scrap. Dana White built his promotional legacy by freezing out athletes who attempt to play matchmaker from their couches. In boxing, promoters constantly get trapped paying massive retainers to elite technicians who believe they are entitled to dictate every single term while taking zero operational risk.

Passing publicly on José Valenzuela was the ultimate signal. When an athlete tells his own paymasters that he refuses an in-house clash with a dangerous puncher, he ceases to be a promotional asset and becomes an obstacle. If Zuffa cannot use him to test their own talent or build compelling company events, they are simply subsidizing an ego trip.

Cutting ties via a contractual exit would send a message to the rest of the roster that the money requires reciprocal cooperation. If Shakur wants to wait around for perfect conditions at his leisure, he can do it as a free agent on somebody else’s dime.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Denies Teofimo Lopez February 6 Talks
Sports.content:
Update: Ryan Garcia has denied knowing about any negotiations for a February 6 fight with Teofimo Lopez at Madison Square Garden. Ryan responded to a post repeating Chris Mannix’s report by stating, “This is not true. No discussions, at least from my side, has had that. Unless I don’t know about them, but I’m not looking to fight in NY, even though I’m not totally taking that off the table.”

That leaves open the possibility that representatives discussed the date without Ryan’s involvement, but Mannix’s description made the talks sound further along than Ryan believes they are. Between Ryan’s denial and Teofimo’s unresolved Catterall obligation, February 6 now looks more like an idea being circulated than an active fight plan.

This is not true no discussions at least from my side has had that. Unless I don’t know about them but I’m not looking to fight at in NY even tho I’m not totally taking that off the table https://t.co/t8cPLh25gm — RYAN GARCIA (@RyanGarcia) September 22, 2026

Ryan Garcia vs. Teofimo Lopez Talks Target February 6

Ryan Garcia faces a choice between taking a December date with Isaac Cruz or holding out for a clash with Teofimo Lopez. The second route is complicated by Lopez’s mandatory WBA obligation involving Jack Catterall.

Cruz called for Ryan after stopping Nestor Bravo in six rounds Saturday night in San Diego. Ryan quickly accepted and indicated that an offer would follow.

Preliminary discussions have taken place between representatives for Ryan and Lopez. Chris Mannix revealed that talks have targeted February 6, 2027, at Madison Square Garden.

“There have been conversations between the representatives of Garcia and Lopez about making a Garcia versus Lopez fight, to the point where the conversations even got to a spot where they talked about a date, which is early February. I think February 6th is the date that I was told, and the location is Madison Square Garden in New York City,” said Mannix on his channel.

Mannix prefers Ryan to skip Cruz and go directly into the Teofimo bout. That route assumes the WBA will permit Lopez to bypass Catterall, who defeated Shakhram Giyasov to secure his mandatory claim.

Matchroom has sent formal legal letters urging the sanctioning body to enforce its ruling. Eddie Hearn argues that Catterall’s status carried over with the belt from Rolando Romero to Teofimo. Team Lopez claims the directive applied strictly to Romero and no longer binds the new titleholder.

Mannix’s February target ignores the governing body timeline. Unless Ryan meets Teofimo prior to Catterall’s cited November window, Teofimo must satisfy that mandatory defense. Negotiations, a potential purse bid, a full camp, and physical recovery would make February 6 impractical.

Catterall also represents a stylistic danger for Teofimo. The British southpaw controls distance with a disciplined jab, employs lateral movement and scores with counters without retreating into a shell. He has a clear blueprint in Shakur Stevenson’s showing against Teofimo. Teofimo relies on a predictable pattern. He presses forward like an incoming tide to unleash combinations before resetting straight back. That approach gives a poised counterpuncher like Catterall clean opportunities to time him. Teofimo risks losing the belt before Ryan ever gets him in the ring.

If Teofimo chooses to vacate instead, the matchup with Ryan loses its title prestige and strips Teofimo of negotiating power. Ryan generates massive arena business on his own name. Lopez relies on Ryan to produce a career-high purse.

Waiting on Teofimo introduces ring rust for Ryan. Lengthy layoffs have disrupted Ryan’s timing throughout his career, and sanctioning body disputes rarely resolve quickly. A December fight keeps him sharp while cashing another substantial check.

Pitbull Cruz brings action appeal, yet remains vulnerable to Ryan’s weapons. The short pressure fighter moves forward behind an earmuff guard and lunges inside. Ryan possesses the straight right to split that defense and the check left hook to catch Cruz in mid-leap. That physical contrast grows sharper once Ryan hydrates up into middleweight territory on fight night.

Teofimo delivers the steeper tactical hurdle. He possesses the lateral agility to circle away from Ryan’s hook, the upper body slip to evade incoming right hands, and the counterpunching ability to punish an upright target.

Mannix viewed Cruz as a distraction on the road to Lopez. Catterall stands as the real roadblock. Ryan can face Cruz in December while Lopez sorts through his WBA mess. If Teofimo still possesses the belt when the dust clears, Madison Square Garden will still be waiting.

The WBA already shredded its own credibility by sanctioning Teofimo against Rolly Romero in the first place. Giving an immediate shot at a secondary belt to a fighter coming straight off a wide points loss to Shakur Stevenson made a mockery of the ratings. The only justification offered was the commercial value of putting two loud talkers on pay-per-view.

Now Gilberto Mendoza is caught in the trap he created. That July 9 message to Catterall, explicitly telling him he would get the winner of Rolly versus Teofimo within 180 days, puts the WBA president on the record. Matchroom’s legal team has documented proof that Catterall took the risk, beat Shakhram Giyasov, and earned his status in a sanctioned eliminator.

From a sporting standpoint, letting Teofimo bypass Catterall looks terrible. It signals that mandatory positions only exist for contenders who lack the leverage to be ignored. Teofimo arguing that his name was not on the original paperwork is classic promoter double-talk. Mandatory obligations belong to the championship belt, not the individual holding it. If a title changes hands, the new champion inherits the baggage attached to the hardware.

Despite how ugly it looks, the WBA will almost certainly look for an escape hatch if Ryan Garcia and Lopez finalize terms. Sanctioning bodies operate on percentages of total fight purses. A percentage of a Ryan Garcia pay-per-view at Madison Square Garden generates massive revenue for the WBA. A low-profile mandatory defense between Lopez and Catterall in Manchester or New York pays a tiny fraction of that amount.

Ghana News.title: COPEC backs possible transport fare increase but warns of impact on commuters
Ghana News.content:
The Executive Director of the Chamber of Petroleum Consumers (COPEC), Duncan Amoah, says some increase in transport fares may be justified as operators continue to grapple with rising fuel and maintenance costs.

Speaking in an interview on JoyNews, he said the government’s GH¢2 per litre intervention on diesel has helped sustain fuel prices for transport operators but has not fully offset the rising cost of operations.

According to him, the Ghana Private Road Transport Union (GPRTU) has been engaging stakeholders for several months over its request for a fare adjustment.

He argued that given the financial pressures facing commercial drivers, “it is only fair that some amount of increase be allowed to the driving community.”

Mr Amoah said he would expect the ongoing discussions between the GPRTU and government to result in a lower adjustment than the 30% increase initially proposed by the union.

“I would be surprised if they come back and say they could not reach an agreement. I would expect maybe 15, 20 percent by the close of the engagement,” he said.

He stressed, however, that the figure was his expectation rather than an agreed fare adjustment.

Mr Amoah also acknowledged that any increase in transport fares would ultimately affect commuters, whose incomes have largely remained unchanged.

“The end payer is going to bear the brunt because salaries have not been increased,” he said.

He therefore suggested that discussions on transport fares should be accompanied by broader consideration of workers’ incomes, with organised labour playing a role in negotiating possible adjustments to salaries.

Mr Amoah further called for a more scientific approach to determining transport fares, proposing that the GPRTU and the Transport Ministry develop a cost-per-kilometre and cost-per-passenger model.

He said such a system would allow fares to be calculated objectively based on factors such as distance, fuel consumption, vehicle maintenance and passenger numbers, rather than being determined through negotiations alone.

Ghana News.title: Dr. Nyaaba calls for sustainable transport and organic inputs to support farmers
Ghana News.content:
A former Director of the Peasant Farmers Association of Ghana (PFA), Dr Charles Nyaaba, is making a strong case for greater investment in sustainable transport systems and environmentally friendly agricultural inputs to help farmers reduce production challenges.

He says inadequate transportation from farms to markets continues to leave many farmers stranded with their produce, particularly in farming communities where access to reliable transport remains limited.

Speaking at the Ecobank-JoyBusiness Financial Dialogue Series, Dr Nyaaba said innovative transport solutions, including battery-powered vehicles, could help improve the movement of farm produce from production centres to markets.

He cited the use of rechargeable battery-powered yards as an example of how alternative energy solutions could be adapted to support agricultural communities.

“How can we make such transport system available to most of the farmers who are stranded in the farm gate?”

Dr Nyaaba said improving transport infrastructure and systems at the farm-gate level would help farmers move their produce to nearby markets and ultimately connect them more efficiently to consumers.

He also raised concerns about farmers' continued dependence on chemical pesticides and fertilizers, stressing the need to improve access to organic alternatives.

According to him, although organic fertilizers and pesticides are gradually entering the market, challenges remain with their quality, availability and uptake among farmers.

“Majority of farmers today still depend on chemical pesticides and fertilizers,” he said, adding that access to organic alternatives remains a major challenge.

Dr Nyaaba therefore called for greater support for the development and distribution of quality organic fertilizers and pesticides, as well as financing mechanisms that can make such products more accessible to smallholder farmers.

He said a broader approach to green financing should address not only renewable energy for agricultural production but also sustainable transportation and environmentally friendly farm inputs.

Such interventions, he noted, could help reduce the environmental impact of agriculture while improving farmers' ability to transport their produce, lower production costs and access markets.

Ghana News.title: MTN Ghana to extend earnings into second-half of 2026; share price going for GH₵6.69
Ghana News.content:
MTN Ghana is expected to extend its earnings into the second-half of 2026 on the back of a strong earnings growth outlook supported by its data and fintech businesses.

According to analysis by Databank Research, the management's elevated capital expenditure programme, largely directed towards network modernisation, additional spectrum deployment and capacity expansion, should improve network quality and support continued growth in high-value data subscribers amid rising digital adoption.

“We also expect the merger of MobileMoney Limited and MobileMoney Fintech Limited to accelerate product innovation and deepen ecosystem integration, strengthening fee income generation while improving operational efficiency”, it mentioned

It believes MTN Ghana remains well positioned to deliver another period of robust gains, adding, its defensive earnings profile, strong cash generation and dividend credentials should continue to underpin investor appetite and support further re-rating despite its strong year-to-date performance of 66.67%.

The share price of MTN Ghana is presently going for GH₵ 6.69.

Its year-to-date return stands at 59.3%.

MTN Ghana recorded a profit before tax of GH¢7.4 billion in the first-half of 2026.

This was an increase of 44.5% over the GH¢5.1 billion posted in the first half of 2025.

Service revenue also reached GH¢14.9 billion from GH¢11.3 billion recorded last year, representing a 32.3 % growth.

Ghana News.title: Bono Region faces doctor shortage as only 7 of 20 posted doctors report – Deputy Health Minister
Ghana News.content:
Only seven of about 20 doctors posted to the Bono Region have reported for duty, highlighting concerns over the availability and retention of medical personnel in the region.

Deputy Minister of Health, Prof. Dr Grace Ayensu-Danquah, disclosed this during a courtesy call on the Bono Regional Coordinating Council (RCC) as part of her working visit to the region.

Prof. Ayensu-Danquah was accompanied by a delegation led by the Chief Executive Officer of the Sunyani Teaching Hospital, Dr Cardinal Newton.

The visit was aimed at engaging key stakeholders and assessing some of the challenges affecting healthcare delivery in the Bono Region.

During the meeting, the Deputy Minister, on behalf of the Bono Regional Health Directorate, appealed to the RCC to provide support to the health sector through the mobilisation of funding, resources and other interventions.

She said such support would help strengthen healthcare delivery and improve the quality of services available to residents.

Prof. Ayensu-Danquah identified inadequate accommodation as one of the major challenges affecting the deployment and retention of health professionals in the region.

She therefore called for closer collaboration between the health authorities and the RCC to address the challenges confronting the sector, particularly those affecting the availability of medical personnel.

Bono Regional Minister, Joseph Addae Akwaboa, Esq., assured the delegation of the RCC’s commitment to supporting the health sector.

He pledged to work with relevant authorities to provide the necessary assistance within the RCC’s capacity to address challenges confronting healthcare delivery in the region.

The Regional Minister also expressed appreciation to Prof. Ayensu-Danquah and her delegation for the visit and wished them a successful and productive working engagement in the Bono Region.

Ghana News.title: Mahama to cut sod for 160-bed referral hospitals in Oti, Savannah and Western North
Ghana News.content:
President John Dramani Mahama will, in the coming weeks, cut the sod for the construction of three 160-bed Regional Referral Hospitals in the Oti, Savannah and Western North Regions, Government Communications Minister Felix Kwakye Ofosu has announced.

According to Mr Kwakye Ofosu, the projects form part of the government’s broader strategy to improve healthcare delivery in Ghana by expanding critical health infrastructure and increasing access to quality medical services across the country.

The Minister made the announcement in a Facebook post on Tuesday, September 22, while sharing the architectural design for the proposed regional referral hospital in the Oti Region.

He said the facility will form part of the government’s efforts to strengthen healthcare infrastructure and improve access to referral services for residents in the region.

The planned sod-cutting ceremonies for the three hospitals will mark the commencement of projects expected to provide additional capacity for specialised and referral healthcare services in the Oti, Savannah and Western North Regions.

Mr Kwakye Ofosu said the initiative reflects President Mahama’s broader commitment to improving healthcare infrastructure as part of the government’s development agenda.

Ghana News.title: Dr Kwame Nkrumah’s birthday celebration: Africa must heed Nkrumah’s vision of unity – Prof. Lumumba
Ghana News.content:
Prof. PLO Lumumna (2nd from right) making a remark at the ceremony. Those with him are Johnson Asiedu Nketia (left), National Chairman of the NDC; Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah (2nd from left), Minister of Lands and Natural Resources, and other dignitaries

African leaders have been urged to return to the founding ideals of intercontinental unity by Ghana’s first President, Osagyefo Dr Kwame Nkrumah.

A renowned Pan-Africanist and Kenyan legal luminary, Prof. P.L.O. Lumumba, said 66 years after independence, Africa remained politically divided and economically colonised amid its enormous natural resource endowment.

He described the situation as a betrayal of Nkrumah’s vision of a united Africa, which must be reversed.

Prof. Lumumba was speaking at this year’s NkrumahFest celebration at Nkroful, the birthplace of Dr Nkrumah in the Western Region, last Saturday, on the theme: Nkrumah at 117, celebrating his enduring legacy – Africa must unite or perish.”

NkrumahFest is an annual heritage and cultural festival to honour the legacy, vision, and birth anniversary of Dr Nkrumah, which was spearheaded by the Member of Parliament (MP) for Ellembelle, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah.

The celebration, which started last Friday, saw the unveiling of a roundabout with the statue of Dr Nkrumah in the Ellembelle District in the Western Region.

The event was attended by the Paramount Chief of Essikado Traditional and President of the Western Regional House of Chiefs, Nana Kobina Nketsia V; the former running mate of the New Patriotic Party (NPP) in the 2024 general election, Dr Matthew Opoku Prempeh; the daughter of Osagyefo Dr Nkrumah, Samia Nkrumah, and a Pan-Africanist and veteran journalist, Kwesi Pratt Jnr.

Others included some members of the political divide and guests from various parts of the country and the world.

Prof. Lumumba said Nkrumah’s vision for a united, dignified Africa remained relevant and intergenerational decades after his death.

He described Dr Nkrumah as one of the greatest Africans to have lived, saying his contribution to the liberation and dignity of Africa went far beyond his country of birth, Ghana.

Dr Nkrumah dedicated his life to restoring the dignity of Africans and reminded the continent that its political independence could only be protected through African unity.

Prof. Lumumba recalled Nkrumah’s advocacy for African unity, including his role in the establishment of the Organisation of African Unity (OAU), now the African Union, in 1963 in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

He also recalled the historic moment when Nkrumah warned that if African countries failed to unite, the forces that had previously colonised the continent could return in different forms.

Independence and sovereignty

Prof. Lumumba further referenced Nkrumah’s book “Africa Must Unite”, saying it reflected his strong conviction that African countries needed to work together to protect their independence and sovereignty.

He linked Nkrumah’s Pan-African vision to the civil rights struggle in the US, saying Ghana became an important source of inspiration for leaders such as Martin Luther King Jr., among many others.

He said although Nkrumah’s political career was cut short following the 1966 coup, attempts to suppress his legacy could not extinguish his ideas even after death.

The remains of Dr Nkrumah were first interred in Guinea, moved to Nkroful, and later to the current resting place in Accra.

The convener of the event, Mr Buah, who is also the Minister of Lands and Natural Resources, said Nkrumah’s legacy should inspire renewed commitment to self-determination, Pan-Africanism and shared prosperity, particularly among the younger generation.

The country under the regime of Nkrumah, he said, saw the establishment of major institutions of learning, infrastructure projects such as the Akosombo Dam, the Tema Harbour, the Adomi Bridge and factories, among many other investments which could best be described as intergenerational.

Ghana News.title: Dr Nyaaba calls for green financing to help farmers switch to solar-powered irrigation
Ghana News.content:
A former Director of the Peasant Farmers Association of Ghana (PFA), Dr Charles Nyaaba, is calling for targeted green financing schemes to help farmers replace fuel-powered irrigation systems with solar-powered alternatives.

He says rising fuel costs and changing weather patterns are pushing more farmers to rely on irrigation to sustain production, particularly during the off-season.

Speaking at the Ecobank-JoyBusiness Financial Dialogue Series, Dr Nyaaba said financial institutions and other stakeholders must design support systems that will enable farmers to acquire solar-powered pumping machines.

He noted that many farmers currently use ordinary water pumping machines powered by fuel, a situation which adds significantly to their production costs.

According to him, moving to solar-powered irrigation could reduce the cost burden on farmers while also contributing to efforts to reduce carbon emissions from agricultural activities.

“What kind of support system can we put in place for these farmers who use ordinary water pumping machines to now begin to use solar-powered pumping machines, renewable energy?”

Dr Nyaaba said the need for such interventions has become more urgent as some farmers are increasingly shifting production towards the off-season due to their recent experiences with changing weather conditions.

He explained that access to affordable renewable energy could make it easier for farmers to continue production while reducing their dependence on fuel.

He therefore urged banks and other financial institutions to consider agricultural financing products specifically designed to support investments in renewable energy technologies.

Dr Nyaaba said green financing should not be limited to large businesses and projects but must also reach smallholder farmers, who form a significant part of Ghana's agricultural sector.

He believes financing solar-powered irrigation could simultaneously address production costs, climate-related challenges and the country's broader efforts to transition towards more sustainable agricultural practices.

Ghana News.title: Investor sentiment towards banking stocks to remain positive
Ghana News.content:
Investor sentiment towards banking stocks is expected to remain positive, supported by dividend payouts across most listed banks.

According to the Databank Research 2026 Half-Year Outlook, the resumption of dividend payments, following regulatory approval, reflects significantly stronger capital buffers, strong profitability despite lower interest rates, with sector net income growth of about 4% between first-halves of 2025 and 2026.

Additionally, there is enhanced asset quality, signaling the sector's continued recovery from the effects of the Domestic Debt Exchange Programme (DDEP).

The report stated that although non-performing loan (NPL) ratios remain above the Bank of Ghana’s regulatory threshold for some banks, it expects asset quality to improve further as credit conditions normalise and recovery efforts gain momentum through the remainder of the year.

The sector’s Non-Performing Loans (NPLs) declined to 16.1% in half-year 2026 from 23.1% in half-year 2025, reflecting early signs of balance sheet repair.

“We expect banks to intensify loan recovery initiatives and work towards the central bank’s 10% regulatory threshold by year-end, in line with the stipulated deadline”, Databank Research explained.

Half-year banking stocks Y-T-D performance

It added that the capital adequacy has also strengthened across the sector, rising to 20.4% in half-year 2026 from 19.7% in half-year 2025, underscoring a more resilient banking system with stronger capacity to absorb potential macroeconomic and credit shocks.

It continued that its analysis favour banks with strong capital positions, improving asset quality and resilient profitability.

"Although lower interest rates may compress net interest margins over 2H’26 [Second-half year 2026], we expect disciplined loan growth, and growing credit demand will support earnings momentum. In our view, improving macro conditions, stronger earnings visibility and dividend resumption suggest further upside through 2H’26.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
