A Venezuela IMF office will open in Caracas next year, possibly in the first half of 2027, Kristalina Georgieva said on Monday. The fund’s chief spoke after meeting Delcy Rodríguez, Venezuela’s acting president, in New York on 21 September 2026.

The International Monetary Fund lends to governments in financial trouble and monitors their economies. Rodríguez is due to meet Donald Trump on Tuesday 22 September, on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly.

What Georgieva promised

Georgieva told Bloomberg News the plan for a Venezuela IMF office would become a reality. It could open sometime in the first half of next year, she said.

Bloomberg had earlier reported that Venezuela had begun sharing more economic data with the fund.

Georgieva said the fund was now making sure it caught up quickly on Venezuela’s data and on key monetary and fiscal policies.

The IMF resumed dealings with Venezuela on 16 April 2026, after a break that began in 2019. IMF officials visited Caracas in late July, the first such trip in more than two decades, Bloomberg reported.

Georgieva wrote on social media that Monday’s talks focused on recovery and reconstruction after this year’s earthquakes, Reuters reported.

A day of meetings with lenders

Rodríguez arrived in New York early on Monday, on her first trip to the United States since taking office in January. John Barrett, the top US diplomat in Venezuela, met her at the airport, state television said.

She first met Ilan Goldfajn, president of the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB), the main regional development lender. She then saw Georgieva and Ajay Banga, president of the World Bank, in separate meetings.

The talks took place at Venezuela’s mission to the United Nations, the Argentine news site Infobae reported. Calixto Ortega, her vice president for the economy, joined her with hydrocarbons minister Paula Henao and foreign minister Félix Plasencia.

Goldfajn told Reuters the IDB is drawing up a two-year plan for Venezuela, focused partly on electricity and social protection. Venezuela owes the bank about US$2.5 billion, according to Infobae.

Debt is the larger theme. “Her visit will have a big focus on debt restructuring, funds and payments,” one source told Reuters.

Venezuela said in May it would restructure the debts of the state and of the state oil company, PDVSA. Most analysts put those debts at US$150 billion to US$200 billion, Reuters reported.

António Guterres at UN headquarters in New York on 13 October 2016, shortly after his election as secretary-general, in a file photograph (Photo by Drew Angerer/Getty Images)

Guterres and the path to democracy

Later on Monday, Rodríguez met UN Secretary-General António Guterres at UN headquarters. A UN statement said they discussed economic reforms, debt restructuring, dialogue initiatives and cooperation with Caracas.

That cooperation covers human rights, “as well as the path toward a full democracy,” the statement said, as quoted by Reuters.

Rodríguez told the state broadcaster VTV that Venezuela came seeking “peace, stability, human development, and global balance of all kinds,” AFP reported. She is due to address the General Assembly on Wednesday 23 September 2026.

Why the Trump meeting matters

Rodríguez was vice president to Nicolás Maduro, whom US forces seized in Caracas in January. Maduro is awaiting trial on drug-trafficking and other charges in a federal prison in New York.

Since then she has cooperated with Washington, including on access to Venezuela’s oil reserves, the largest in the world. Mike Waltz, the US ambassador to the UN, said the meeting would take place at a reception Trump hosts.

It would be the first meeting of the two countries’ leaders since Maduro briefly met Barack Obama in 2015, Infobae noted.

Lula’s warning

Brazil’s president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, criticised the relationship in an interview with CNN International in New York on Monday. The Spanish news agency EFE summarised his view: Washington conveys the idea that it now governs Venezuela.

“The country’s sovereignty is over,” Lula said, in EFE’s account. He added that this was not good for the United States, for Venezuela or for democracy.

He said Rodríguez should call a national election. “The way the United States treats Delcy, it looks like it is her boss,” he said, according to EFE.

Lula is seeking re-election in Brazil’s vote on 4 October 2026. He asked Washington not to interfere in that contest, EFE reported.

Two polls, two stories

Venezuelan state-aligned outlets on Monday and Tuesday recirculated a Hinterlaces poll showing 91% support for dialogue with Washington. Hinterlaces is a Caracas pollster whose results are regularly promoted by state media.

The survey was first published on 7 September. It found 91% rated the dialogue with the United States positively, 6% negatively and 3% gave no answer.

Hinterlaces interviewed 700 people, with a stated margin of error of 3.5 percentage points, the state-aligned site La Iguana reported.

Another pollster, Meganálisis, whose published commentary sharply questions Rodríguez’s legitimacy, found 91% disapproved of Trump meeting her. Only 4% approved, the Miami newspaper El Nuevo Herald reported.

Its online survey of 1,627 adults ran from 15 to 19 September. It also found 80% opposed the oil agreement that Washington and Caracas signed on 28 August.

The two firms asked different questions, by different methods, about two weeks apart.

What comes next

Rodríguez meets Trump on Tuesday and speaks at the General Assembly on Wednesday. Sources told Reuters the visit is expected to produce agreements on energy, debt and mining.

For the fund, the next marker is the Caracas office, which Georgieva said could open in the first half of 2027.

More: Venezuela coverage, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is Delcy Rodríguez?

Delcy Rodríguez is Venezuela’s acting president. She was vice president under Nicolás Maduro and took over after US forces seized him in Caracas in January 2026. Maduro is awaiting trial in New York. Washington has since worked with her government on oil, sanctions and debt.

Why is the IMF opening an office in Caracas?

The IMF resumed dealings with Venezuela on 16 April 2026 after a break that began in 2019. Georgieva told Bloomberg News the Venezuela IMF office will open next year, possibly in the first half of 2027. She said the fund was catching up quickly on the country’s data and its monetary and fiscal policies.

What did Lula say about Venezuela?

In an interview with CNN International on 21 September 2026, Brazil’s president said the country’s sovereignty was over, according to EFE. The agency summarised his view as saying Washington conveys the idea that it governs Venezuela. He urged Rodríguez to call a national election.

Do Venezuelans back the rapprochement with Washington?

Polls disagree because they measure different things. Hinterlaces, whose results state media promote, found in early September that 91% viewed the dialogue positively. Meganálisis, critical of Rodríguez, found in mid-September that 91% disapproved of her meeting Trump.

Sources: Reuters on the New York meetings, debt talks and the UN statement, El Espectador on Georgieva’s remarks to Bloomberg News, Bloomberg on the IMF office, Infobae on the lenders and Guterres, AFP on the arrival and the General Assembly speech, EFE on Lula’s CNN interview, La Iguana on the Hinterlaces survey, Correo del Orinoco on the 7 September release, El Nuevo Herald on the Meganálisis poll, IMF on resuming dealings with Venezuela

World.title: Argentina: Rodrigo de Loredo Takes Over Córdoba’s Radical Party
World.content:
Argentina · Politics

Key Facts — What happened Allies of Rodrigo de Loredo won the Radical party’s Córdoba city committee vote on Sunday 20 September 2026.

— The result Legislator Miguel Nicolás took almost 59% against about 41% for Pablo Farías, backed by rival Ramón Mestre.

— How the province was won A national electoral court ruling on 17 September 2026 left De Loredo’s faction as the only list for provincial leadership.

— The catch Only about 8,000 of roughly 68,000 party members voted in the city, according to Perfil.

— Why it matters De Loredo aims to lead a broad anti-Peronist alliance into Córdoba’s 2027 governor election.

— What comes next Matías Gvozdenovich takes over as provincial party president at the end of September.

A low-turnout party vote and a court ruling have put one man’s faction in charge. It now runs the Radical party in Córdoba, Argentina’s second most populous province. His target is the 2027 race for governor.

Córdoba Cathedral and the Cabildo in the historic centre of Argentina’s second-largest city. File photograph. (Photo: Rio Times media library)

Rodrigo de Loredo now controls the Radical party in Córdoba, the Argentine province he wants to govern from 2027. His allies won the party’s city vote on Sunday 20 September 2026.

That vote followed a court ruling three days earlier that handed his faction the provincial leadership without a contest. Together they give him the party machinery for a run at the governorship.

The Radical Civic Union, known by its Spanish initials UCR, is one of Argentina’s oldest parties. In Córdoba it remains the main organised force outside Peronism, the movement that runs the province.

A clear win on a small turnout

Sunday’s main contest was for the UCR’s committee in Córdoba city, Argentina’s second-largest city. Letra P, a political news site, calls it the party’s most important post in the city.

Miguel Nicolás, a provincial legislator from De Loredo’s Generación X faction, took almost 59% of the vote. Pablo Farías, candidate of the rival Más Radicalismo alliance, won just over 41%.

The financial daily Ámbito and Letra P reported those figures. De Loredo’s camp put the split at 60% to 40%, according to the newspaper Perfil.

Participation was thin. Perfil reported about 8,000 voters from a roll of 68,000 party members, a turnout of roughly 12%.

La Política Online, a political news site, reported doubts over whether turnout had reached the 10% minimum required for internal UCR votes.

De Loredo celebrated on the social network X. “Enormous victory in the primaries of our political organisation,” he wrote, claiming wins in 12 of the city’s 14 party districts.

The rival camp did win one prize. In Colón department, Luis Carrizo of Más Radicalismo beat Ezequiel Lemos, mayor of Río Ceballos, by 1,317 votes to 913.

The provincial party was settled in court

The bigger prize, the provincial committee, never went to the ballot box. On Thursday 17 September 2026 the National Electoral Chamber rejected an appeal by Más Radicalismo.

The chamber is Argentina’s top court for electoral matters. It ruled the appeal had been wrongly admitted, without deciding the underlying complaints, Perfil reported.

That left standing a lower-court decision by federal electoral judge Miguel Hugo Vaca Narvaja. Generación X became the only valid list for the provincial leadership.

According to Ámbito, Más Radicalismo had filed lists in 18 departments, but ten were challenged. That left it below the minimum of 14 departments the party rules require.

A ballot box used in Argentina’s national elections, labelled by the district electoral board (Junta Electoral Nacional). File photograph. (Photo: Rio Times media library)

Matías Gvozdenovich, who leads the UCR group in Córdoba’s provincial legislature, will therefore become party president. He takes office at the end of September, Ámbito reported.

Ramón Mestre, a former mayor of Córdoba city who leads Más Radicalismo with Juan Jure, rejected the outcome. He said the new leadership came from a process “lacking transparency and founded on the proscription of the opposition”, the regional newspaper Puntal reported.

Juan Jure, the faction’s candidate for the provincial presidency, has said it will not recognise the new party authorities, Ámbito reported. He added that it will field its own candidate for governor and is weighing a Supreme Court appeal.

Why Córdoba matters beyond the province

Córdoba had 3.84 million inhabitants at the 2022 census, second only to Buenos Aires province. It is a farming and industrial heartland, and a prize in any national election.

Peronists have governed the province for nearly three decades. Governor Martín Llaryora heads the current administration, which has drawn some Radicals into its coalition.

Among them is Vice-Governor Myrian Prunotto, who came from the UCR. The new leadership has vowed to stop further defections.

Gvozdenovich wrote on X on 21 September: “Now, together with Miguel Nicolás, we are going to de-Peronise Radicalism. And next year, with Rodrigo de Loredo, de-Peronise Córdoba.”

The road to 2027

De Loredo, a former national deputy, has lost a major race before. In 2023 he ran for mayor of Córdoba city and lost to the Peronist Daniel Passerini.

Passerini took 47.72% to De Loredo’s 39.98% in the provisional count, according to the Córdoba TV channel El Doce.

He has not formally launched a campaign. Ámbito reported that he told his inner circle, “I am going for the governorship.”

Ámbito says he wants President Javier Milei’s party,La Libertad Avanza, and Senator Luis Juez’s Frente Cívico in one alliance. Both are rivals as well as potential partners.

La Libertad Avanza’s leading local figure is national deputy Gabriel Bornoroni. Juez has been a force in provincial politics for more than 20 years.

De Loredo’s strongest asset is the party’s network of mayors. In June, more than 60 Radical mayors and local leaders backed his bid for governor, Ámbito reported.

That network is not fixed. Ámbito noted that six mayors in San Justo department have agreed to move to La Libertad Avanza.

For now, De Loredo’s faction holds both the city and provincial party committees. Whether that is enough to lead a united opposition in 2027 will be decided with his rivals, not his party.

More: Argentina coverage, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What office did Rodrigo de Loredo win?

None personally. His ally Miguel Nicolás won the Radical party’s Córdoba city committee on 20 September 2026. Another ally, Matías Gvozdenovich, becomes provincial party president after a court ruling on 17 September 2026. De Loredo leads the Generación X faction that now controls both committees.

What is the UCR?

The Radical Civic Union, or Unión Cívica Radical, is one of Argentina’s oldest parties. It is a centrist force that has produced several presidents. In Córdoba it is a leading opposition party, with around 120 mayors, according to Ámbito.

When is the Córdoba governor election?

Córdoba elects its next governor in 2027, the same year as Argentina’s presidential election. The province sets its own election calendar. Governor Martín Llaryora heads the current Peronist administration.

Did the rival faction accept the result?

No. Ramón Mestre, who leads the rival Más Radicalismo alliance, said the new leadership came from a process lacking transparency. The National Electoral Chamber rejected his faction’s appeal on procedural grounds, without ruling on the complaints themselves.

Sources: Perfil on the city vote and turnout, Ámbito on the result and the governorship plan, Letra P on the city and Colón results, La Política Online on turnout and alliances, cba24n on the party’s new leadership, Perfil on the electoral court ruling, Puntal on the ruling and Mestre’s response, El Doce on the 2023 mayoral result

World.title: AMIA Bombing: Argentine Judge Charges 8 Over 1994 Jewish Centre Attack
World.content:
Argentina · Justice

Key Facts — What happened Federal judge Daniel Rafecas issued a 648-page ruling on 21 September 2026 charging eight men over the 1994 attack.

— Who is accused Four men who held top Iranian posts in 1994, two former diplomats, an alleged intelligence agent and an alleged Hezbollah operative.

— A sitting commander One accused, Ahmad Vahidi, has commanded Iran’s Revolutionary Guard, its elite military force, since 1 March 2026.

— The money Rafecas ordered a freeze of US$500 million on the assets of each of the eight accused.

— Why it matters It moves the case closer to Argentina’s first trial in absentia, which Rafecas ordered in June 2025.

— The catch None of the accused is in Argentina, the ruling can be appealed, and no trial date has been set.

A truck bomb killed 85 people at a Jewish centre in Buenos Aires 32 years ago. Now a federal judge has formally charged eight men in their absence. None is in custody, and none has been convicted.

The Palace of Justice in Buenos Aires, seen at dusk behind the Lavalle monument. File photograph. (Photo: Rio Times media library)

The AMIA bombing case, over the 1994 attack on a Jewish centre in Buenos Aires, has taken its biggest step in years. On Monday 21 September 2026, federal judge Daniel Rafecas formally charged seven Iranians and a Lebanese man over the 1994 attack.

The truck bomb destroyed the Buenos Aires headquarters of the Asociación Mutual Israelita Argentina (AMIA), the country’s main Jewish community centre. It killed 85 people and injured at least 151, according to federal prosecutors.

None of the eight is in Argentina, and none has been tried or convicted. The ruling relies on a 2025 law that lets some cases proceed without the accused in the courtroom.

What the judge decided

Rafecas is the acting head of Federal Criminal and Correctional Court No. 6 in Buenos Aires. His 648-page ruling, reported by the news site Infobae, is known in Argentine law as a procesamiento.

A procesamiento is not a verdict. It is a pre-trial finding that the evidence is strong enough to send a suspect toward trial, and it can be appealed.

The judge also ordered a freeze of US$500 million on the assets of each accused. Whether any of those assets can be found has not been reported.

The ruling holds that Iran’s top leadership decided on the attack in August 1993. It says execution was entrusted to Hezbollah, the Lebanese armed group allied with Tehran.

The eight accused

Four men who held senior Iranian posts in 1994 were charged as indirect perpetrators, meaning those who allegedly ordered the crime. Two are Ali Fallahijan, then intelligence minister, and Ali Akbar Velayati, then foreign minister.

The other two are Mohsen Rezai, then commander of the Revolutionary Guard, and Ahmad Vahidi, then head of its Quds Force. The Quds Force runs the Guard’s operations abroad.

Vahidi now leads the whole Revolutionary Guard, Iran’s elite military force. He was appointed on 1 March 2026, after his predecessor was killed in the US-Israeli war on Iran.

Three more were charged as necessary accomplices. They are Hadi Soleimanpour, then Iran’s ambassador to Argentina, and Mohsen Rabbani, then cultural adviser at the Iranian embassy.

The third is Ahmad Reza Asghari, described in the ruling as a Revolutionary Guard intelligence agent. The eighth accused is Salman Raouf Salman, also known as Samuel El Reda.

Rafecas accused Salman, a Lebanese citizen, of coordinating the final stage of the attack for Hezbollah. Two other suspects, Abdallah Salman and Hussein Mouzannar, were not charged for lack of evidence.

Iran has never accepted the Argentine accusations. In 2007 Interpol issued red notices, its international wanted-person alerts, for several of the men.

A synagogue in Buenos Aires. File photograph. (Photo: Rio Times media library)

How the attack unfolded, according to the ruling

The ruling says the attackers bought a Renault Trafic van on Sunday 10 July 1994. It was loaded with about 300 kilograms of ammonal and TNT, two types of explosive.

The van was left in a public car park four blocks from the building on Friday 15 July. It was driven to the centre on the morning of Monday 18 July, when the building was busiest.

The judge classified the attack as a crime against humanity and as genocide under international law. The charges include aggravated homicide and injury motivated by racial or religious hatred.

Rafecas also linked the attack to a bombing of a passenger plane in Panama on 19 July 1994. That blast killed 20 people, 12 of them members of Panama’s Jewish community.

Why a trial without the accused is now possible

For three decades the AMIA bombing case stalled because the accused stayed abroad. Argentine law did not allow them to be tried in their absence.

Law 27,784, published in the Official Gazette on 7 March 2025, changed that. It allows trials in absentia for crimes including genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes and terrorism.

In April 2025 prosecutor Sebastián Basso, head of the special AMIA investigative unit, asked Rafecas to apply the law. His request covered ten suspects, all of whom the court had formally declared fugitives for failing to appear.

Rafecas granted the request on 26 June 2025, the first time the law was applied in Argentina. A federal appeals chamber upheld his decision on 23 September 2025.

Not every victims’ group backs the procedure. Memoria Activa and two other associations of victims’ relatives opposed it in 2025, Infobae reported.

The public defender’s office challenged the law as unconstitutional. On the same Monday, the Federal Criminal Cassation Chamber, Argentina’s top criminal appeals court, rejected that challenge.

One of its three judges was Carlos Mahiques, the father of Justice Minister Juan Bautista Mahiques.

What the government said

Justice Minister Juan Bautista Mahiques welcomed the ruling on the social network X. He called it “a historic step” for the 85 victims, their families and Argentine society.

“Soon there will be an oral trial in Argentina for these facts,” he wrote, according to the news site El Destape. His ministry said in a statement that the ruling marked “a milestone in the fight against impunity”.

Patricia Bullrich, the senator who leads the bloc of La Libertad Avanza, President Javier Milei’s party, also backed the law on social media. “If a terrorism suspect flees, justice does not stop,” she wrote.

Bullrich also criticised the agreement on the case that Argentina signed with Iran under former president Cristina Fernández de Kirchner. She said the new law “came to end impunity”.

What happens next

The ruling can be appealed by the public defender, Hernán Silva, according to Infobae. If higher courts confirm it, the judge can ask the parties whether to send the case to trial.

That trial would be held before a federal oral court, Argentina’s trial-level criminal bench. No date has been set.

Rafecas also asked the Supreme Court to consider merging the case with the 1992 bombing of Israel’s embassy in Buenos Aires. Prosecutors argue the same organisation carried out both attacks.

For the victims’ families, the AMIA bombing case has been a story of delay since 1994. The minister’s promise of a trial now depends on the appeals courts.

More: Argentina coverage, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What was the AMIA bombing?

On 18 July 1994 a van bomb blew up outside the headquarters of the Asociación Mutual Israelita Argentina (AMIA) in Buenos Aires. The centre was the main institution of Argentina’s Jewish community. The attack killed 85 people and injured at least 151, according to federal prosecutors.

Have the accused been convicted?

No. Judge Daniel Rafecas issued a procesamiento, a pre-trial finding that there is enough evidence to move toward trial. It can be appealed, and the accused are presumed innocent. None of the eight is in Argentine custody, and Iran has never accepted the accusations.

What is a trial in absentia?

It is a trial held without the defendant present. Argentina allowed it through Law 27,784, published on 7 March 2025. It covers crimes including genocide, crimes against humanity and terrorism, when suspects have been formally declared fugitives. A public defender represents them, and a defendant who later appears can in some cases request a new trial.

Who are the accused?

Ali Fallahijan and Ali Akbar Velayati were Iran’s intelligence and foreign ministers in 1994. Mohsen Rezai and Ahmad Vahidi were senior Revolutionary Guard commanders. Hadi Soleimanpour and Mohsen Rabbani were diplomats. Vahidi has commanded the whole Revolutionary Guard since 1 March 2026. Also charged were alleged intelligence agent Ahmad Reza Asghari and Lebanese citizen Salman Raouf Salman, an alleged Hezbollah operative.

World.title: Costa Rica Population Could Begin Shrinking Earlier Than Expected
World.content:
Costa Rica’s population could begin shrinking earlier than previously expected as the number of children being born continues to fall faster than population experts had projected. Costa Rica’s fertility rate is now estimated at about 1.12 children per woman in 2026, below the 1.20 that had been expected for this year.

The difference may appear small, but it continues a long decline in births that is rapidly changing the age and size of Costa Rica’s population. In 2025, Costa Rica registered 48,414 births, the lowest number recorded during the past decade. That was 23,933 fewer births than in 2016, meaning it recorded roughly one-third fewer babies last year than it did nine years earlier.

Population projections had already suggested that Costa Rica would begin seeing its total population decline around 2044. The faster-than-expected drop in fertility means that point could arrive sooner. The change is not expected to produce a sudden drop in population. Instead, Costa Rica is gradually moving toward a society with fewer children and young adults and a larger share of older residents.

A fertility rate of about 2.1 children per woman is generally considered necessary for a population to replace itself over the long term without relying on immigration. Costa Rica is now far below that level. The reasons behind the decline are not tied to one single issue. Costa Ricans are waiting longer to have their first child, families are choosing to have fewer children, and a growing number of people are deciding not to become parents at all.

The cost of housing, childcare, employment, household finances and access to support networks can also influence decisions about whether or when to have children. Women are also increasingly delaying motherhood while studying, working and pursuing other personal goals.

Researchers say these are long-term social changes rather than a temporary decline that is likely to quickly reverse. The consequences will become increasingly noticeable in areas ranging from schools to the labor market. Fewer births eventually mean fewer children entering classrooms.

Some rural communities are already dealing with falling school enrollment, and the trend could eventually lead to more school consolidations or closures in areas where there are no longer enough students. Universities will eventually face smaller groups of potential students as well and the workforce will also change.

As today’s smaller generation of children reaches adulthood, fewer young people will enter the labor market to replace workers who retire. At the same time, Costa Rica will have a growing number of older residents requiring pensions, healthcare and other services. That combination could place additional pressure on the Costa Rican Social Security Fund and the country’s pension systems because a smaller working-age population will be helping support a larger retired population.

Costa Rica is already aging quickly as people age 65 and older are projected to make up about 12% of the population in 2026. That proportion is expected to continue rising over the coming decades, while the percentage of children and working-age residents gradually declines.

The demographic change could also affect housing since smaller families and more people living alone or as couples may need different types of homes than one dominated by larger families with several children. Businesses could face changes as well, particularly employers that depend on a steady supply of younger workers.

Immigration could eventually become increasingly important in maintaining Costa Rica’s workforce as the number of locally born workers declines. Population experts do not describe the falling birth rate as an immediate crisis, but rather as a major demographic change that Costa Rica will have to prepare for.

Costa Rica still has time to adjust, particularly by improving education, employment opportunities and productivity among the working-age population it already has. But the latest fertility numbers suggest that the transition is happening faster than expected. Costa Rica is not simply experiencing a year or two with fewer babies but is moving toward a future in which there will be fewer young people, more older adults and, eventually, fewer residents overall.

World.title: U.S. Deported More Than 25,000 People Through Secret Third-Country Deals
World.content:
The United States deported more than 25,000 people under secret agreements with 35 countries to receive migrants who have no ties to those nations, according to an investigation published Monday. Since President Donald Trump took office in January 2025, the United States has signed agreements with developing countries to accept migrants who cannot legally be sent back to their countries of origin.

The investigation by the nonprofit organization Forbidden Stories revealed that the government allocated $410 million to be paid directly to receiving countries or to United Nations agencies to facilitate the deportations. At least 25,447 people were deported to third countries through August 31, 2026, according to data compiled by Forbidden Stories together with a consortium of international journalists.

The vast majority, about 20,000, were sent to Mexico, while the rest were distributed among 27 other countries in Latin America, Africa and the Pacific. Agreements were also finalized with seven additional countries. The agreements vary, including which nationalities may be deported and whether people with criminal records can be accepted.

Legal limbo

An investigation published earlier this year revealed that Washington has been using visa bans and restrictions against African countries to pressure them into accepting deportees. Lawyers said that deportees were being placed in a “legal limbo,” detained without charges in countries with which they have no ties and where they have few rights, if any.

Forbidden Stories reported that 49 of Africa’s 54 countries had been contacted to determine whether they would accept deportees from third countries. A little-known division of the State Department, the Office of Remigration, created in May 2025, handled most of the negotiations and payments, according to the same source.

The office is headed by Christian Jove Ehrhardt, a 41-year-old diplomat who previously worked as a security officer. The report details his visits to Cameroon, which signed a memorandum of understanding with the United States in December to accept deportees. One week later, it also signed a five-year health assistance program worth nearly $400 million.

The following month, the State Department said it would provide another $30 million to the UN Refugee Agency, UNHCR, in Cameroon to “facilitate the voluntary return of refugees and combat illegal immigration.” The first plane carrying deportees arrived in Cameroon on January 14.

Payments

Other agreements include direct payments to governments. Palau, a small Pacific island nation with a population of fewer than 18,000 people, signed an agreement in December 2025 to accept up to 75 third-country nationals in exchange for $7.5 million. So far, however, only three people have been sent under the agreement.

In Eswatini, 32 people have arrived since July 2025, out of a potential total of 160 contemplated under an agreement worth more than $5 million. According to the investigation, the country agreed to accept deportees with criminal records.

Of the $410 million budgeted for the agreements, internal State Department documents showed that $81 million was intended for the governments that signed them. The remainder was earmarked for aid organizations, including more than $178 million for the UN’s International Organization for Migration, or IOM, and $123 million for UNHCR.

The agencies have faced criticism over their involvement, although UNHCR told Forbidden Stories that it was not a party to the bilateral agreements and that U.S. funding was being used in accordance with its mandate to strengthen asylum systems. An IOM spokesperson told Forbidden Stories that the agency’s decisions to accept funding were based “on a single question: whether our involvement will improve the lives of the migrants affected. In these cases, we firmly believe that it will.”

World.title: Costa Rica’s Two-Century Fight to Keep Its Orchids
World.content:
For nearly two centuries, Costa Rica’s forests have drawn collectors chasing the same prize. It has one of the richest orchid floras on the planet, with estimates running from about 1,500 to nearly 1,700 species, and a large share of them grow nowhere else on earth.

That rarity, paired with a market willing to pay heavily for the right bloom, has made Costa Rica a persistent target for plant smuggling. The trade reaches back well before Costa Rica had any law to stop it and the story begins with the guaria morada. In the 1830s George Ure Skinner, a British trader based in Guatemala, collected Central American plants and shipped them to England, feeding the Victorian craze for tropical orchids.

English botanist James Bateman named the purple orchid Cattleya skinneri in his honor. Botanists have since reclassified it as Guarianthe skinneri, though most Costa Ricans still know it simply as the guaria morada. In 1939 President León Cortés Castro declared it the national flower. The honor did nothing to slow demand, and decades of collecting badly depleted wild populations. Conservationists have spent years repropagating and reintroducing it, along with its yellow-flowered relative Cattleya dowiana.

Lycaste orchids tell a similar story as several species in the genus are found only in Costa Rica, and collecting pressure has pushed some, including Lycaste dowiana, into steep decline in the wild, prompting repropagation efforts to restore them. The main international tool against this trade is CITES, the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species. Signed in 1973 and in force since 1975, it now has more than 180 member countries, Costa Rica among them.

Every orchid species falls under CITES, most in the category that requires export permits, with the rarest given the same top-tier protection as tigers and great whales. The treaty’s record on orchids is disputed since some botanists argue it has done little to prevent extinctions. They point out that news of an upcoming stricter listing can set off a rush of collecting before the rules take effect, while slow permitting for legitimate research often lags behind the pace of habitat loss.

The people doing the collecting work far from any courtroom. In Costa Rica they are known as materos, and they operate deep in cloud forests and jungles, hunting rare and newly described species for an international orchid market valued in the billions of dollars. Smuggling methods have ranged from hidden vehicle compartments to suitcases packed with live plants to shipments accompanied by falsified paperwork.

Orchids are not the only target as Cycads, an ancient plant group prized by collectors for their slow growth and rarity, are among the most trafficked plants in the world. One American collector who visited Costa Rica in 1979 later recalled gathering Zamia seeds because seeds could leave without the export permit a live plant required, and said enforcement at the time was lax enough that whole plants would hardly have been harder to take.

The problem extends beyond wild plants. When Costa Rica passed its plant breeders’ rights law in 2008, legislative records cited earlier cases of Colombian rice varieties and Canadian and Dutch potato varieties being used without authorization, part of the argument that Costa Rica needed a formal system to protect breeders and meet its trade obligations.

The trade is far from historical as authorities seized 4,366 animal and plant specimens at Costa Rica’s main airports and border crossings between 2024 and 2025, according to the Judicial Investigation Agency’s forensic biology section. Orchids were among the plants recovered, and in one case more than 300 were found in a single traveler’s luggage.

John Vargas, head of that forensic biology section, has said the number of wildlife cases referred for scientific identification has risen by 330 percent since 2023. Those figures helped prompt #WhatYouCarry, a campaign launched in late July by Humane World for Animals, the Judicial Branch and airport operator AERIS. It asks travelers to take home photographs and memories rather than pieces of the country’s biodiversity.

Nearly two centuries after Skinner’s first shipments left Central America, demand for Costa Rica’s orchids has not faded. What has changed is the effort to protect them, from international treaties to airport inspections to greenhouse repropagation, all racing against a trade that has never really stopped.

World.title: International News: California declares State of Emergency ahead of potential record-strength El Niño
World.content:
International News: California declares State of Emergency ahead of potential record-strength El Niño

By Zoila Palma: Today, California Governor Gavin Newsom declared a statewide state of emergency as officials prepare for a potentially historic El Niño weather event that could bring severe winter storms, flooding, landslides, and coastal erosion.

The governor’s office said state resources are being mobilized to strengthen preparedness and protect vulnerable communities ahead of the expected weather impacts.

Under the emergency proclamation, state agencies are directed to stage flood-fighting supplies, including sandbags and pumps, prepare critical infrastructure, and position equipment along roads at risk of flooding and snow-related disruptions.

The California National Guard may also support flood response, search-and-rescue, engineering, and logistics operations, while environmental agencies will work to accelerate preparations for landslides and debris flows.

California Office of Emergency Services Director Caroline Thomas Jacobs said officials are taking action before severe weather arrives, ensuring that communities and first responders have the personnel, equipment, and support needed to respond to changing conditions. Newsom said the emergency declaration is intended to provide communities with additional support and families with greater confidence that the state is prepared for severe weather.

El Niño is a climate pattern involving unusually warm ocean temperatures in the central and eastern tropical Pacific, which can influence weather patterns across the United States and other regions.

World.title: International News: US, China discuss AI safety mechanism ahead of Trump-Xi Summit
World.content:
International News: US, China discuss AI safety mechanism ahead of Trump-Xi Summit

By Zoila Palma: The United States and China are exploring the creation of a notification mechanism to report artificial intelligence incidents that could affect national security, as officials from the two countries held economic and trade discussions ahead of a planned summit between Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Sunday that senior US and Chinese officials discussed the proposed AI notification system during what he described as “successful” talks with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng in New York.

The meeting comes as Trump and Xi prepare to meet in Washington later this week, BBC reports.

Bessent emphasized the importance of transparency between the world’s two leading AI powers, arguing that potential risks linked to artificial intelligence require greater communication across borders. His comments follow recent warnings from researchers about AI’s potential dangers and calls from prominent technology figures for more cautious development of the technology.

Beyond AI safety, the discussions also covered trade issues, including plans to operationalize a process known as the Board of Trade to identify potential tariff reductions on goods.

World.title: United States of America congratulates Belize on 45th anniversary of Independence
World.content:
United States of America congratulates Belize on 45th anniversary of Independence

By Zoila Palma: Today, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio congratulated Belize on the 45th anniversary of Independence.

“On behalf of the United States of America, I extend my warmest congratulations to the people of Belize as you mark the 45th anniversary of your nation’s independence.

The United States values the enduring friendship and close collaboration between our two countries, and we commend Prime Minister John Briceño’s dedication to strengthening regional security and promoting sustainable economic growth. We look forward to continuing our partnership with Belize in building a more secure and prosperous future for both our peoples,” Rubio said.

The USA and Belize established diplomatic relations in 1981 following Belize’s Independence.

Belize remains a committed partner on U.S. regional priorities, including security, prosperity and governance, democracy and human rights, migration management, and climate change.

World.title: International News: War, AI threats and Climate crisis to dominate UN General Assembly
World.content:
International News: War, AI threats and Climate crisis to dominate UN General Assembly

By Zoila Palma: World leaders are gathering at the United Nations this week as ongoing wars, artificial intelligence risks, climate change, and global economic pressures take center stage during the annual General Assembly meeting.

Conflicts in Gaza, Ukraine, Iran, Sudan, the Democratic Republic of Congo, and Myanmar are expected to feature prominently in discussions, with leaders facing questions about how international cooperation can help end violence and address humanitarian crises.

Climate-related disasters, rising living costs, disrupted shipping routes, and growing inequalities are also expected to shape the agenda, AP reports.

Meanwhile, concerns over the potential dangers of rapidly advancing artificial intelligence have added to discussions about global security and humanity’s future.

The future of the United Nations is also expected to come under scrutiny, including proposals to reform institutions such as the Security Council, where the United States, Russia, China, Britain, and France hold veto power.

The selection of a successor to Secretary-General António Guterres, whose second term ends on December 31, 2026, is another issue drawing attention. The 81st General Assembly’s official theme is “Restoring trust, managing transformation: A United Nations that delivers for all.”

Despite the divisions and challenges facing the international community, the United Nations remains a key platform for dialogue among its 193 member states.

The high-level debate, scheduled to begin on September 22, provides an opportunity for world leaders to discuss cooperation, peace, development, and collective responses to global crises.

World.title: PM Briceño: “Build a Belize where every generation has the opportunity to thrive”
World.content:
PM Briceño: “Build a Belize where every generation has the opportunity to thrive”

By Zoila Palma: Prime Minister John Briceño has called on Belizeans to reflect on the country’s progress and remain committed to building a brighter future as Belize celebrates its 45th Independence anniversary.

“As we celebrate 45 years of Independence, let us honour how far we have come, believe boldly in how far we can go, and continue building a Belize where every generation has the opportunity to thrive,” Briceño stated.

Happy Independence Day Belize!

World.title: Leader of Opposition: “We celebrate our shared heritage”
World.content:
Leader of Opposition: “We celebrate our shared heritage”

By Zoila Palma: Today, Leader of the Opposition Tracy Panton joined in extending Independence Day wishes to all Belizeans.

“Today, we celebrate our shared heritage, the remarkable journey that brought us here, and the limitless promise of tomorrow. United by our love for Belize, strengthened by our diversity, and inspired by a common purpose, let us stand together and build a brighter, more prosperous future for every Belizean.

With courage in our hearts, hope in our vision, and unity as our greatest strength, we can move Belize forward, from strength to strength,” Panton expressed.

Panton called for our “national pride to shine brighter than ever, may progress reach every community, and may the spirit of unity guide us toward a future filled with opportunity, peace, and promise.”

Long live BELIZE!

World.title: 62 year old retiree punched twice in the mouth at Orange Walk gas station
World.content:
62 year old retiree punched twice in the mouth at Orange Walk gas station

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police in Orange Walk are investigating a reported assault in which a 62 year old retiree was allegedly punched twice in the mouth at a gas station on Friday night.

According to police information, the incident happened at around 8:45 p.m. at the 24/7 Gas Station on Belize Corozal Road.

The complainant told police that a man known to him approached while he was standing near the store.

According to the report, the complainant attempted to offer the man marijuana, but the man allegedly became aggressive and said he did not want anything.

The complainant said he stepped back, but the man allegedly approached and punched him once in the mouth.

He said that after questioning why he had been hit, the man returned and allegedly punched him a second time in the mouth.

The complainant reportedly began bleeding from his mouth and later made a report to police officers who were in the area.

He was taken to the police station and issued a medico legal form.

A doctor later classified his injuries as wounding.

Police identified the person of interest as Roberto Antunez, 36, a labourer of Orange Walk Town.

Police say charges for wounding are pending.

World.title: Central American Integration System Sec-Gen congratulates Belize on 45th Anniversary of Independence
World.content:
Central American Integration System Sec-Gen congratulates Belize on 45th Anniversary of Independence

By Zoila Palma: Today, the Secretary General of the Central American Integration System (SICA) extended congratulations to Belize on its 45th anniversary of Independence.

“On September 21, 1981, the Belizean people celebrate their history, identity, and diversity.

As a member country of the Central American Integration System (SICA), we recognize its valuable contribution to building a more united, integrated, and supportive region,” SICA said.

World.title: ‘Pastor shot me twice’
World.content:
SMITH... was pastor of Pathways International Restoration Ministries in Albion, St James

A witness broke down in tears on Monday while recounting the terrifying ordeal of being shot twice in the back by his late pastor, Dr Kevin Smith, who had assured him that he was immortal and could not die.

The witness, who also testified that Smith emptied two firearm magazines at members of the security forces on October 17, 2021 at Pathways International Restoration Ministries in Albion, St James, received permission from Justice Leighton Pusey to remove his shirt in court to show the scars from the ordeal.

Last week, the witness told the court that Smith had another member of the congregation stab him in the back. He also used the opportunity, while he was shirtless, to point to the area of his back where he had been stabbed.

Monday was the witness’s second day on the stand in the Home Circuit Court murder trial in Kingston of Andre Ruddock, who is accused of killing 39-year-old Taneka Gardner during an alleged human sacrifice ritual at the church on October 17, 2021.

Ruddock allegedly acted on the instructions of Pastor Smith, who had asked Gardner if she believed that he could bring her back to life if her throat was cut.

Gardner’s throat was subsequently cut, allegedly by Ruddock, after she gave an answer in the affirmative to Smith’s question.

The witness had testified that after Gardner’s throat was cut, Smith further instructed Ruddock to cut her head off. It was alleged that while Ruddock was doing as he was instructed, a cow broke loose from a section of the church property and Ruddock’s attention was shifted from Gardner after Smith gave more instructions for the cow to be caught and slaughtered. A member of the church allegedly chased the cow.

The witness, Gardner, and Ruddock were members of Smith’s congregation.

The witness recalled Smith walking over to him while he was on the ground in agony and stuffing his fingers in his wounds.

“I was saying, ‘I am in pain, I am in pain.’ I remember he walked over to me. I don’t remember him speaking but I can remember him pushing his fingers in the wounds in my back. On the compound, there were a lot of individuals sitting on the boardwalk. The persons he [Smith] had called to come in, they were also sitting on the boardwalk. I looked up and I saw my mom sitting there,” the witness said.

He also testified that police and soldiers came to the boardwalk.

“One of the soldiers was kicking me in my side. He was saying to me that I was shooting at him. I told him I wasn’t doing that, and a police officer came and said to the soldier to ‘Stop, don’t you see that he was shot and cramped?’

“The soldiers started ordering the other [church] members outside, telling them to hold their heads straight. They were very hostile. An ambulance came and the police assisted them to wrap my back. They placed me on a stretcher and brought me through the side gate that was there,” the witness said, explaining that Gardner’s body was still laying on the church compound at that time.

“Taneka’s body was there. Blood was there. I was able to see. I was laying face down on the stretcher so I was able to see because the compound was not dark. When I was going through the gate, I saw Andre Ruddock on the ground. He was laying on his side. I also saw Dr Smith on the ground with his hands behind him. There was nothing blocking my view. Kevin Smith was laying face down. Security forces were all over the compound. At the gate there were police and soldiers. I was taken to the Cornwall Regional Hospital,” he told the court.

The witness said Smith was the one who shot him with a firearm he had taken from a member of the church.

“There were like three police jeeps on the outside of the premises. They were opposite the gate on the other side. At that time, a police officer was climbing on the fence [to see what was happening]. Mr Smith started to say he was Elijah and he was saying just as Elijah called down fire from heaven to consume the army, he said ‘If I be a prophet of God, I call down fire from heaven to consume these 50. He said it like three times, and he then called out for a member of the Jamaica Constabulary Force who was there [as a member of the church]. She came to him and he spoke to her and she spoke back to him,” the witness said.

By that time, Gardner was already killed, allegedly by Ruddock.

The witness, who was asked by lead prosecutor LaToya Bernard to tell the court what happened after the member of the police force spoke to Smith, explained that the pastor used the gun he had received from the member of the church to open fire at the security forces who were outside the compound of the church.

“Dr Smith started shooting at the police. At that time I stepped away and went right behind a round column that was there when Dr Smith took the gun from her. I could see him firing the gun from behind the column. He was firing the gun towards the police. I wasn’t observing everything happening on the compound. I was mainly watching him and was wondering if the police were going to shoot back,” the witness told the court.

“That was why I was behind the column. When I was looking towards where the police were I could see police bending down. I did not see them return any fire. After that happened, Dr Kevin Smith then called [the police member of the church] to bring an extra magazine [for the gun]. Dr Smith continued to fire. The police did not retaliate. Outside the premises there were members from the congregation out there along with the police. Those members on the outside weren’t running or moving or anything at all. They were just out there,” the witness testified.

He said the next thing he remembered after Smith shot at the security forces were loud explosions at the gate where the police shot and killed a member of the church who was following Smith’s instructions to attack them with a knife.

After he put his shirt back on, the witness, who had been standing during his testimony, was given an opportunity to sit and compose himself while he cried.

“Yes, Mr Kevin Smith shot me. I can remember hearing loud explosions coming from right beside me, where Mr Smith was. I fell to the ground after I felt like I got a hard punch. I remember jumping up back like I was shocked. He looked on me and said to me that, ‘You are immortal and you cannot die’. Yes, that’s what he said. I could see some police officers standing at the top of where a boardwalk was. They were on the premises by this time.

“Mr Smith then spoke to Kevaughn Plummer. I can’t recall where Andre Ruddock was at the time when Dr Smith was firing at the police. Dr Smith spoke to Kevaughn Plummer and he ran towards the police to attack them. He had a knife and he ran towards them to attack them. Upon reaching close proximity to the police, I just started seeing fire coming from the police’s gun. I could hear the loud explosions. I saw when Kevaughn Plummer’s body fell to the ground. It happened so quickly. It was just a lot of shots being fired all over the compound. By that time, because of the pain I was feeling, I was laying flat on my belly at that time on the boardwalk. I was hearing a lot of shots. At that time I turned my head and saw him [Dr Smith] sitting in the same place where he was sitting when we first came up the boardwalk. He was sitting and pointing to the sky,” the witness said.

Pastor Smith died on October 25, 2021 in a motor vehicle crash on the Linstead bypass in St Catherine while being transported to Kingston to face charges.

World.title: Morotcycle mayhem
World.content:
In this file photo Inspector Amos Thompson points to a number of motorcycles that were seized by the Westmoreland police.

WESTMORELAND is recording one of its lowest murder counts in years but police say the parish is facing another public safety threat involving motorcycles, prompting a call for tougher national measures to tackle dangerous riding.

Commanding officer for the division, Senior Superintendent Othneil Dobson said the police will continue seizing and prosecuting offenders but believes the country must change its approach to the motorcycle problem.

The call comes as Westmoreland records a 29 per cent reduction in murders between January 1 and September 12, with the number falling from 28 in 2025 to 20 this year.

But while the division works to maintain the reduction in violent crime, Dobson said motorcycle-related crashes remain a persistent road safety concern, particularly in a parish where motorcycles are widely used as a means of transportation.

Speaking during a recent episode of the Jamaica Constabulary Force’s Force4Good Podcast, Dobson said the police have been carrying out daily enforcement operations, supported by specialised teams, but dangerous riding continues to result in fatalities.

“I would not sit here and tell you that most of the persons are obeying the road traffic law. Most of the accidents are a result of careless driving, persons not having the best will or thinking about the other road users. So, we have high numbers of fatalities — but it’s not a lack of trying from the police,” he said.

Dobson reported the police have recorded some success, but the recurring nature of motorcycle crashes means enforcement must be accompanied by broader public education and changes in how Jamaica manages the issue.

“As a country, we’ll have to change some of what we’re doing with motorcycles. Most of the stations in Westmoreland are overrun with motorcycles… You seize 20 or 30 bikes and you’re driving to work the next morning and you see four or five persons riding past you with new bikes. They don’t even come back to the stations to retrieve the bikes after going through the licensing process again,” he said.

“So, as a country, we have to go from a policy perspective in terms of dealing with this bike situation. We will continue to seize, we will continue to prosecute, we will continue to educate… but the penalties just have to be higher penalties as it relates to bikes,” he argued.

World.title: Love & Harmony turns 10 with a family affair at sea
World.content:
The Love and Harmony entertainment package for 2027 will include: (clockwise from top left) Aidonia, I-Wayne, D’Yani, Kevin Downswell, Beres Hammond and Sanchez.

For a decade, Love & Harmony Cruise has been bringing Caribbean music lovers together on the high seas. Next year the celebration is getting even more personal as the popular music cruise marks its 10th anniversary.

With a special Mother’s Day voyage scheduled from May 6 to 11, 2027, the whole family will be invited to celebrate a milestone that has become as much about community as it is about music.

Reggae icon Beres Hammond will be captaining the ship once more and, as it has done for the past nine years, the Love and Harmony crew expects to deliver an unforgettable experience on the high seas.

Veteran Beres Hammond will be joined by Sanchez, D’Yani, Aidonia, Kevin Downswell, and I-Wayne for the special anniversary sail dates, with more artistes and entertainment still to be announced.

The six-day, five-night experience will be a round trip from Miami aboard the Norwegian Jewel, making stops in Montego Bay, Jamaica, and Nassau, Bahamas.

But while the 10th anniversary promises the concerts, parties, and entertainment that guests have come to expect, organisers are placing a special emphasis on family this time around.

“Ten years is an incredible milestone for Love & Harmony, but what makes this anniversary even more meaningful is that we are sailing over Mother’s Day weekend,” Director of Marketing and Public Relations Ronnie Tomlinson said.

“Love & Harmony Cruise has always felt like a family reunion at sea. We have guests who return year after year, and this time we want them to bring their mothers, children, and loved ones and celebrate together. This is more than a cruise, it is six days of Caribbean culture, music, food, laughter and memories,” he said

That family-friendly approach is reflected in the offer for the 2027 sailing, with children 12 and younger sailing for free, subject to applicable taxes and fees.

And for those who have experienced Love & Harmony before, the promise is familiar: Once the ship leaves Miami, the party does not stop simply because the sun goes down.

Live concerts, themed parties, DJ experiences, karaoke, games, comedy, poolside activities, and the Captain’s Dinner will fill the schedule, while Caribbean flavours will remain an important part of the experience.

Guests can expect a mix of Caribbean and American fare alongside Norwegian Jewel’s fine and casual dining options, with Jamaican favourites such as oxtail, ackee and saltfish, jerk chicken, and curry goat among the flavours that have helped bring the island experience aboard.

While music remains the heartbeat of Love & Harmony, laughter has increasingly become part of its soundtrack and as such comedy will play a big part in the cruise’s itinerary come May. Canadian comedian Trixx will return following his appearance on the 2026 sailing, while Jamaican-British comedian White Yardie will make his Love & Harmony debut. The comedy offering adds another layer to a voyage that has evolved beyond a traditional music cruise, giving guests something to do whether they are catching a concert, lounging poolside, or simply looking for a reason to laugh.

The anniversary celebration makes its way back to Jamaican soil when the Norwegian Jewel docks in Montego Bay on Saturday, May 8. Love & Harmony will take over Tropical Bliss Beach for a special destination experience hosted by dancehall star Aidonia, giving guests the chance to trade the ship for sand, sea, and the unmistakable energy of Montego Bay. The ship is scheduled to be in port from 10:00 am to 4:00 pm, allowing Harmonisers to spend the day experiencing Jamaica before returning to the vessel and continuing the anniversary festivities.

Then, on Sunday, May 9 — Mother’s Day — the ship will remain at sea.

For organisers, the timing is intentional.

Rather than rushing from one destination to another, families will have the entire day to celebrate together, surrounded by music, food, entertainment, and the community that Love & Harmony has cultivated over the past decade.

The cruise will then head to Nassau, Bahamas, on May 10 before returning to Miami on May 11.

With additional artistes, DJs, special events and anniversary surprises still to be announced, the 2027 sailing is shaping up to be both a look back at Love & Harmony’s first decade and a celebration of the people who helped make the journey possible.

World.title: THE HUNDRED THAT WASN’T ENOUGH
World.content:
Jayden Seales of Antigua and Barbuda Falcons celebrates the dismissal of Kirk McKenzie of Jamaica Kingsmen during the Republic Bank Caribbean Premier League Final on Sunday.

JAMAICA Kingsmen Captain Rovman Powell said he was proud of his team despite an eight-wicket defeat to Antigua and Barbuda Falcons in the Republic Bank Caribbean Premier League final at Kensington Oval in Bridgetown, Barbados, on Sunday.

Antigua and Barbuda Falcons needed just 16.4 overs to chase down Kingsmen 170-9 and win their first-ever Republic Bank Caribbean Premier League (CPL) title, turning Maaz Sadaqat’s brutal 114 from 58 balls into a footnote.

“It’s a good feeling, to be honest. I think it’s a very hard-fought campaign for us. I’m so proud of the boys,” Powell said in a televised interview.

Batting first after losing the toss, Kingsmen were 30-2 in the fourth over before Sadaqat exploded. The left-hander hammered nine sixes and eight fours in a stunning hundred, adding 80 runs for the third wicket with Saim Ayub (29) to surge to 100-2 after 10 overs where it looked like the Kingsmen would have reached the 200-run mark.

However, the Falcons’ left-arm spinner Sufyan Moqim produced the spell of the tournament — four for 14 runs from four overs — and ripped the guts from the Kingsmen’s innings. After Ayub’s dismissal at 110-3 in the 12th over, no Kingsmen batsman made double figures.

Powell said his side fell short with the bat in the second half of their innings.

“I think after the halfway stage we felt as if we were 10 to 15 runs short,” Powell admitted.

“We knew it was a pretty good batting wicket. Credit has to be given to our batters for the first 10 overs. Maaz played fantastically for us, and the partnership he strung with Saim Ayub carried us to 100 for 2 in 10 overs. It’s disappointing that as a batting group on such a good wicket we didn’t really capitalise on that start,” he further said, hailing Ayub’s removal of Rakheem Cornwall (20) at 20-1 in the first over, and Evin Lewis’s (38) fall to Vitel Lawes at 84-2 in the eighth over.

Despite these feats, however, the chase was a demolition as

Amir Jangoo (57 not out) and Hasan Nawaz (47 not out) never looked troubled as they finished the job with 20 balls to spare.

“I think as a batting group, when we lost four wickets in the middle overs, four key batters who were supposed to put the impetus on the game in the last 10 overs, and as a bowling group, we didn’t control the powerplay as well as we wanted to,” Powell said.

But for Jamaica, a team that lost its first few games and was written off, Powell said that the final itself was redemption.

“I honestly feel it’s a proud journey for us. We have accomplished a lot of things. We set out to be in the finals, and when we came to the tournament we wanted to see if we could progress all the way. It was a slow start to the competition, as we lost our first few games, but we built a little bit of momentum with our home crowd back home in Jamaica and from there the guys started to believe that we could actually play cricket,” Powell said.”

“We went to Trinidad, which is a difficult place to play cricket, and we played a very good game down there. That confidence kept building within the team. We knew that as soon as we squeezed into the last four of the competition how dangerous our team could be, and the guys just kept chipping in. Credit has to be given to them throughout the entire competition. They listened to the leadership that myself and the head coach provided and I am actually proud of the boys,” he said.

World.title: BAILEY’S OUT!
World.content:
Jamaica footballer Leon Bailey (Photo: Garfield Robinson)

WITH the Jamaica’s Reggae Boyz eyeing a spot in the knockout stages of the Concacaf Nations League, they will have to do so without winger Leon Bailey who has withdrawn from the entire group stage campaign.

Bailey, who recently signed for perennial Greek champions Olympiakos FC, was one of the marquee names in interim head coach Rudolph Speid’s 24-man squad and was due to join the group on Monday, ahead of their opening game against Guatemala at the National Stadium on Friday.

Although the Jamaica Football Federation (JFF) made no official announcement on Bailey’s withdrawal, Bailey didn’t arrive on the island and will stay in Greece as he recovers from an injury.

The 29-year-old has reportedly been suffering with the injury since playing just over 13 minutes in Olympiakos’s 2-1 win over Jagiellonia Bialystok in the UEFA Europa League last Thursday. Bailey missed the club’s Sunday’s Super League Greece clash against Levadiakos.

Greek journalist George Stasinopoulos played down the severity of the injury but said, “Olympiacos came to an agreement with the medical staff of the Jamaican national team, with both sides coming to an agreement and ultimately Leon Bailey not getting on the plane to make the trip for his national team.

“He suffered from injuries last season and faced several issues, so they have decided to pay enough attention to the Jamaican and take advantage of the break.”

Europa League champion Bailey will miss not only Friday’s game against Guatemala and Monday’s clash with Honduras at the National Stadium, but also the away fixtures against El Salvador next Friday and Honduras on October 5, which will complete Jamaica’s Group B fixtures in Nations League A.

It’s the second-consecutive season where he’s missed the national team’s group stage campaign, having missed all four games in 2024 against Cuba, Honduras (twice) and Nicaragua.

Bailey, who has seven goals in 41 caps for the Reggae Boyz, also missed the entirety of last year’s final round of Concacaf World Cup Qualifiers after picking up several injuries during his short loan spell at AS Roma in Serie A. Jamaica ultimately finished runners-up behind Curacao, and missed automatic qualification to the 2026 FIFA World Cup in United States, Mexico and Canada.

The former Aston Villa winger did feature in the World Cup play-offs in March against New Caledonia and DR Congo but has missed 17 of Jamaica’s last 28 competitive fixtures.

The Jamaica Observer has learnt that a replacement for Bailey is set to be announced Tuesday, with Speid and his technical staff still considering their options as late as Monday afternoon.

Last Friday, Speid revealed he scouted 72 players for the Nations League group stage before selecting the final squad. He also said he invited players outside of the initial 24 to train with the squad as part of a scouting mission, but those names haven’t been made public.

Most of the group participated in an activation session on Monday, with the others set to join the team in their first training session on Tuesday at the National Stadium.

The Reggae Boyz need to finish top two in their group to advance to the quarter-finals where they would play one of Concacaf’s top four nations, Mexico, USA, Canada or Panama, which were pre-seeded.

World.title: The Wellness Wedding: How Healthy Living Is Changing the Guest Experience
World.content:
Wedding bar trends are evolving rapidly. Mindful drinking is becoming increasingly common amongst guests, prompting couples to serve elevated zero-proof options.

Weddings have traditionally been celebrations of indulgence — open bars, impressive appetizers, fancy dinners, decadent desserts and late-night comfort food.. But as lifestyles change, so do weddings.

Today’s younger couples are increasingly health-conscious. They drink less, pay more attention to what they eat and are more aware of dietary restrictions and overall wellness. Naturally, those habits are beginning to influence how they entertain their wedding guests.

The result isn’t the completely “healthy wedding”. It is a more conscious wedding experience, where indulgence and enjoyment coexist with choice.

The Bar Is Changing

One of the biggest shifts is at the bar. Not drinking — or simply drinking less — has become increasingly normal, and zero-proof options are moving well beyond basic fruit punch.

Zero-proof spirits, botanical spritzes, alcohol-free sparkling wines and beautifully constructed mocktails can now be presented with the same attention as traditional cocktails. Couples can even create alcoholic and zero-proof versions of their signature drink.

The message isn’t that we don’t drink. It is you don’t have to drink to fully participate in the celebration.

Food Is Becoming Lighter But Not Boring

Wedding menus are changing too. Couples are increasingly balancing fried hors d’oeuvres, heavy sauces and late-night comfort foods with grilled proteins, ceviches, sushi, fresh seafood, vegetable-forward dishes, salads and fruit.

This isn’t about putting wedding guests on a diet. It is about balance.

A Jamaican wedding doesn’t have to abandon jerk, curry or other favourites. Those dishes can sit comfortably beside grilled seafood, roasted vegetables, vibrant salads and fresh tropical fruit. Guests can indulge while still having choices that reflect how they normally eat.

Dietary Consciousness Is Hospitality

Vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free and allergy-conscious options are also becoming part of normal event planning rather than afterthoughts.

Couples can collect dietary requirements through RSVPs, clearly label buffet selections and ensure alternative meals receive the same attention as the main menu. The vegetarian guest should no longer be served whatever the kitchen can quickly assemble after everyone else has eaten.

That is where wellness becomes good hospitality.

Smoking Is Being Reconsidered

Smoking is another part of the guest experience couples are approaching differently. Cigarette and cigar smoke doesn’t have to drift through lounges, dining areas or dance floors simply because a wedding is outdoors.

Designated smoking areas and thoughtfully positioned cigar lounges allow those who want the experience to enjoy it without imposing it on everyone else.

Wellness Beyond the Reception

For destination weddings, wellness can extend across the entire weekend through morning yoga, spa experiences, fresh juice and smoothie stations, healthier welcome amenities and lighter morning-after brunches.

The idea is simple: Enjoy yourself tonight and still feel good tomorrow.

A New Definition of Luxury

None of this means taking the fun out of weddings. Serve the Champagne, cake and late-night comfort food. Just remember that not everyone drinks, eats meat, wants fried food, or smokes.

The strongest interpretation of the wellness trend isn’t restriction. It is choice.

Luxury hospitality has always been about anticipating what guests might want before they have to ask. For today’s couples, that increasingly means creating a celebration where different lifestyles can comfortably coexist.

The modern wedding isn’t becoming less indulgent. It is becoming more considerate — and perhaps that is one of the most meaningful shifts in the modern guest experience.
